operationalisation of all the sanctioned AWCs by August, 2010 as assured by the 
concerned State Governments. 
 
3.3.7 The issue of outreach of ICDS not reaching all the targeted beneficiaries was 
raised by some of the members.  It was pointed out that AWCs at present have been 
opened at Panchayat level only in States like Madhya Pradesh.  Normally, jurisdiction of 
a Panchayat extends upto a number of villages.  As a result, pregnant women and small 
children, finding it difficult to cover the distance between the AWC at Panchayat and 
villages covered by it remain deprived of Supplementary Nutrition.  Similarly, attention 
of the Ministry was also drawn to  women workforce working in tea gardens and their 
children not getting the benefit of ICDS.  Population norms of 800 for one AWCs or 
minimum requirement of habitations having 40 children were not helping the labour 
population, e.g. those employed for sugarcane harvesting or very small habitations of 
labourers and uneducated class having less than 40 children.  The Committee strongly 
feels that all the problem areas pointed ou t by the Members, based on their first 
hand experience of ground realities need to be looked into immediately.  The 
Committee would appreciate if  a survey of these areas as well as other similar areas 
is be taken up by the Minist ry in co-ordination with th e concerned States.  Present 

norm of 40 children for Anganwadies on De mand may also be reviewed, specially in 
case of specific demands for relaxation of the same.   
 
PRE-SCHOOL EDUCATION KITS    
 
3.4.1 Pre-School Education is a critical co mponent under the ICDS Scheme to ensure 
the holistic development of children.  Pre-School Education Kits are procured and 
supplied by States/UTs as per norms.  To strengthen this component of ICDS, cost norms 
for these kits have been revised from Rs.500 to Rs.1000 per AWC per annum from  
2009-10.  The Committee is, however, surprised to note that State-wise status of 
procurement of Pre-School Kits for AWCs in 2008-09 and 2009-10 reveals that large 
number of States/UTs i.e. Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu 
and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, 
Meghalaya, Mizoram and Sikkim have so far failed to provide this vital component to the 
children in AWCs in their States/UTs.  What is  more disturbing is that in States/UTs like 
Chattisgarh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Chandigarh, Dadra and 
Nagar Haveli, Delhi, Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura, procurement process for the Kits is 
continuing for long. In Maharashtra, Kits  for 2009-10 as well as 2008-09 are being 
procured.  In respect of the remaining States, number of procured kits for 2009-10 falls 
short of the requirement or no response has been forthcoming so far. 
 
3.4.2 The Committee is very disappointed with th is state of affairs.  It seems that 
States are not interested in procuring the Pre-school Education Kits for their 
Children.  The Committee would like to point out that these kits are a replacement 
for pre-parental education in nursery school .  They can be considered an important 

tool for enhancing literacy at  the end of class V.  World- wide, it is an established 
fact that children having a certain minimum vocabulary before entering school have 
a higher chance of achieving literacy at the end of class V.   The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that concerted efforts need to be made so as to convince the 
States to include this very crucial component financial assistance for which is 
provided by the Centre.

th and 20th, November, 2009 had

explored.  The Ministry had also requeste d the Thirteenth Finance Commission to 

provide for the construction of Anganwadi Ce ntres in the State allocation and a decision

like to draw its attention to the fact th at the Report of the Thirteenth Finance

been recommended by the Commission, th e Committee strongly feels that the 
Ministry needs to approach the Planning Commission so as to ensure that this

 MANPOWER UNDER ICDS 
3.6.1 The Committee has  also been voicing its concern about shortage of required 
manpower in the operational AWCs.  The Committee was informed that out of 13,56,027 
sanctioned AWCs  as on 31
st December, 2009, the number of operational AWCs was 
11,04,262.  Against the operational AWCs, 10,60,587 AWWs and 10,38,947 Helpers 
were in position. Gaps have been reported by all the States with Andhra Pradesh, Assam, 
Bihar, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Orissa, Rajasthan, Uttar

takes note of the factors like delays in administrative State sanctions and court cases 
behind the gap in the sanctioned and vacant  posts of ICDS functionaries.   The

delays with the concerned State Government s so that the shortfall in the required 
manpower is removed without further delay. 
 
 
 
 

      AWARD SCHEME FOR ICDS FUNCTIONARIES  
  
3.7.1 Anganwadi Workers are the grassroot level implementers of ICDS Scheme who 
are honorary workers from the local community. A Scheme of Awards for these workers 
was introduced by the Government from 2000-01 which includes a national level award 
carrying a cash award of Rs.25,000/- and a citation and at the  State level, a cash award of 
Rs.5,000/- and a citation. 
 
3.7.2 On a specific query in this regard, the Committee was inform ed that awards for 
the years 2006-07, 2007-08 and 2008-09 were under consideration of the Ministry. 
Attempt of the Committee to understand the reasons for this undue delay led to another 
surprising revelation. Process for the awar ds for 2004-05 and 2005-06 started with 
nominations being invited from the State Governments in August, 2005. It took three and 
a half years for awards to be given in February, 2009, reason being late receipt of 
nominations. As a result, selection process for the awardees for 2006-07, 2007-08 and 
2008-09 could be started only after February, 2009. It is more than a year since then and 
names of awardees are yet to be finalised. 
 
3.7.3 The Committee wonders at the lack of interest on the part of State 
Governments in showing a motivational ge sture towards their own workers inspite 
of all the expenses being borne by the Centre. Only effort to be made on their part is 
nomination of probable awardees. Awards are to be given for services rendered 
during a particular year. To facilitate a worker after such a big gap cannot be 
considered motivational in any respect. The Committee, accordingly, enjoins upon 

the Ministry to get this process expedited at  all the levels and fu lfill the objective of 
this positives initiative.  
 
HONORARIUM FOR ANGANWADI WORKERS AND HELPERS 
 
3.8.1 The Committee notes that apart from Rs.1500/- and 750/- p.m. given to AWWs 
and Helpers majority of States are giving additional honorarium to them. However, NE 
States/UT like Nagaland, Mizo ram, Arunachal Pradesh and Bihar, Puducherry, Gujarat 
and Dadra and Nagar Haveli have not come forward with such a gesture so far .  The 
Committee desires that the Ministry should take up the matter with these States to 
ensure better support from them. The Committee has been voicing its concern about 
these key functionaries of ICDS with manifold activities of not only ICDS remaining 
under paid inspite of being entrusted but also NRHM and other campaigns like 
Immunization drive etc. 
 
3.8.2 The Committee welcomes the initiati ves like provision of uniforms for 
AWWs and Helpers and Insurance Scheme. However, these cannot compensate the 
low level of honorarium inspite of being enhanced recently. The fact remains that 
with the cost of living increasing day by day, interest of these grassroot level 
workers performing a very crucial task in taking care of young mothers and little 
children needs to be given the required importance. For this, more contribution 
from both the States and Centre is required. 
 

MONITORING MECHANISM 
3.9.1 One issue which was raised again a nd again by the members during the 
discussions was lack of visible presence of MPs/MLAs, the public representatives in 
the district level monitoring committees of ICDS. Consensus of the Committee was 
that the very presence of MPs/MLAs in such bodies will not only make all the 
implementing agencies alert but would go a long way in ensuring the outreach of 
this Flagship Scheme to the targetted bene ficiaries.  The Committee, accordingly, 
recommends that the Ministry may take necessary action in this regard. 
 
IV. RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL CRECHE SCHEME FOR THE CHILDREN 
OF WORKING MOTHERS. 
 
4.1 The objectives of the Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme for the Children of 
Working Mothers is to provide day care facilities to children of 0-6 years of parents with 
monthly income not exceeding Rs.12,000. S upplementary nutrition, health care inputs 
like immunization, basic health monitoring and recreation are the benefits provided to the 
children.  The scheme is implemented through the Central Social Welfare Board and two 
national level NGOs, Indian Council for Child Welfare and Bhartiya Adim Jati Sevek 
Sangh (BAJSS). 
 
4.2 Allocation for this scheme for the year 2009-10 was Rs. 100.00 crore. 
Expenditure incurred upto January, 2010 is Rs .71.97 crore.  Budgetary Estimates for the 
year 2010-11 for this scheme when compared to last year have been reduced to Rs.70.00 
crore. On a review of the achievement level of the physical targets under the scheme, 
the Committee notes that outreach of this scheme has shown no expansion. Number 

of crèches and coverage of children have remained at the same level. The Committee 
has been persistently advocating for expa nsion of this scheme  which is primarily 
meant to take care of children of working mothers with meagre income. The 
Committee is disturbed to note that instea d of increasing, the coverage of this 
scheme has started showing a downward trend. The Committee finds that during 
2009-10, against a target of 31,718 crèches, only 26,177 crèches could be opened up 
to 31 st December, 2009. As a result, number of  child beneficiaries also stood at 
6,54,425 against a target of 7,92,950 children. 
 
4.3   While trying to analyze the reasons for this reverse progress, Committee’s attention 
was drawn to the fact that out of 31,718 crèches covered under the scheme handled by the 
CSWB and two NGOs, there were complain ts against the func tioning of one NGO i.e 
Bhartiya Adim Jati Sevek Sangh (BAJSS). As a result, control of 5522 crèches being run 
by this NGO was temporaril y transferred to CSWB on 18 th November, 2008. The 
Committee is of the view that deficiencies like improper maintenance of records and 
registers, non-provision of supplementary  nutrition, unsatisfactory coverage of 
children, irregular payment of honorarium to crèche workers, doctors not visiting 
the crèches regularly noticed by the monitoring agencies in the crèches being run by 
BAJSS are of a very serious nature. Th e Committee finds that inquiry into 
complaints against the NGO is yet to be completed by the Vigilance Wing of the 
Ministry. The Committee is of the firm opinion that the inquiry should be completed 
at the earliest, followed by action against all the concerned agencies/authorities. 
 

4.4 The Committee finds that charge of 5522 crèches being run by BAJSS was 
temporarily transferred to CSWB on 18th November, 2008. It has been more that 16 
months since then and CSWB which is alrea dy handling 20,893 crèches continues to 
have the additional charge of 5522 crèches. The Committee wonders whether the 
CSWB has the required manpower to effectively handle the additional 
responsibility. The Committee is somewhat su rprised to note that as per the Annual 
Action Plan 2010-11, around 26,000 creches  benefitting 4,12,875 children are 
targeted to be covered. This target shows a considerable decline when compared 
with achievement of 26,177 crèches with coverage of 6,54,425 children as on 31
st 
December, 2009. This confirms Committe e’s apprehensions about 5522 crèches 
earlier run by BAJSS being non-functional. No other plausible reason seems to be 
there for such a situation. The Committee would like to be apprised about the status 
of all the functional crèches. 
 
4.5 The Committee notes that NIPCCD which was requested to prepare a 
Concept Paper suggesting revision in the existing scheme with a view to restructure 
the scheme, has submitted the paper on 2 nd February, 2010. At present, an internal 
Committee of the Ministry is examining the Report. The Committee notes that the 
Concept Paper has recomme nded major changes in the cost norms, manpower 
requirement, inclusion of new components like Play and Sleeping Material Kit (PSE 
Kit), rent for crèche building, extensive tr aining for the workers and monitoring on 
six monthly basis.  The Committee welcomes these suggestions for improvement 
which were long awaited. The Committee wo uld appreciate if the final decision on 
the Concept Paper is taken at the earliest and approval process is also expedited. 

The Committee notices a major change suggested in the Concept Paper in the 
implementing agencies from CSWB a nd two NGOs to SHGs, Mahila Mandals, 
Women’s’ Organizations, Panchayats a nd Tribal Associations etc. under the 
supervision of the State Governments. The Co mmittee feels that this is a step in the 
right direction. 
V. SCHEME FOR WELFARE OF WORKING CHILDREN IN NEED OF 
CARE AND PROTECTIONS. 
 
5.1 Under the scheme for Welfare of Working Children in need of Care and 
Protection, funds are released to NGOs on a 90:10 sharing basis for providing facilities 
such as non-formal education, vocational training, counseling, stipend, nutrition etc. to 
facilitate their entry into the mainstream of the education system.  At present, 119 
projects of 100 children each are being run in 17 States/UTs in urban areas not covered 
by the Ministry of Labour under its National Child Labour Project. 
 
5.2 The Ministry’s share of grant in each project for a financial year is Rs. 9,33,120/- 
in case the project running in C Class City [Rs.9,60,120/- and Rs.9,43,920/- in case of 
projects running in A and B Class City, respectively].  Due to shortage of funds during 
2009-10, estimated amount of Rs. 120.00 lakhs is required to be reimbursed to on-going 
projects from the budget provision of the next financial year 2010-11.  In addition, about 
138 new project proposals, received from organizations through their respective State 
Governments are pending in the Ministry.  Due to shortage of funds, no proposals could 
be considered/recommended for financial assistance under this scheme.  However, at 
least 10-12 projects are expected to considered by the PSC during 2010-11 for financial 
assistance with an estimated expenditure of Rs. 76.56 lakhs on new projects.  

 
5.3 While analyzing the utilization status of allocated funds for the last two years, the 
Committee finds that against an allocation of Rs. 7.00 crore in 2008-09 and 2009-10, 
expenditure reported is Rs. 8.38 crore and Rs. 7.93 crore (upto 15.03.2010) respectively. 
 The Committee is, however, surprised to note th at number of projects to be assisted 
during this period has remained below the targets.  Against 125 and 130 projects to be 
assisted during 2008-09 and 2009-10,  projects assisted were only 109 and 105          
(upto 15.3.10) respectively.    Budget provision of Rs. 12.50 crore made for 2010-11 is as 
per the projected requirement of the Ministry.  The Committee hopes that with Rs. 1.20 
crore to be reimbursed on account of expenditure in 2009-10, the Ministry will be in 
a position to provide for the ongoing 118 projects as well as 10 to 12 new projects. 
 
5.4 The Committee has been informed that NIPCCD has submitted its final draft 
Evaluation Report on the Scheme for Welf are of Working Children in need of Care 
and Protection to the Ministry on 1
st January, 2010.  The Committee is happy to 
note that as per the Report, more than 90  percent of the centres have been found to 
be providing all important services envisa ged under the scheme.  As a result, about 
50 per cent of children have withdrawn from active work after joining the centre 
and 28.5 per5cent have joined formal education.  The Committee hopes that 
suggestions for improvement like need for strengthening the infrastructure, capacity 
building measures, community involvement, enhancement of financial norms etc.  
would be looked into and necessary corrective measures initiated at the earliest.  
 

VI. INTEGRATED CHILD PROTECTION SCHEME 
6.1 The Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, 
has been launched during the year 2009-10 by merging three existing schemes i.e. 
Programme for Juvenile Justice, Integrated Programme for Street Children and Shishu 
Greh and has also incorporated new interventions. 
 
6.2 The Scheme seeks to improve access to  and quality of child protection services 
(institutional services through shelter ho mes, children’s homes etc.) create public 
awareness about child rights, clearly ar ticulating responsibilities and enforcing 
accountability for child protection, provide  statutory and support service to children in 
difficult circumstances at all government levels like shelters for children, emergency 
outreach services and set up an evidence based monitoring and evaluation system.  The 
Scheme is being implemented mainly through the State Governments/UT 
Administrations, Child Line India Foundation, NIPCCD and CARA throughout the 
country.  So far, only 17 States namely , Andhra Pradesh, Assa m, Chhattisgarh, Goa, 
Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur,  Nagaland, Orissa, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, 
Tripura and West Bengal etc. have signed the MOU with the Ministry.  The State 
Government of Bihar has also agreed to sign the MOU under the scheme. 
 
6.3 BE 2009-10 of Rs. 60.00 crore for the Scheme was reduced to Rs.50.00 crore at 
the RE stage. This reduction was because most of the  States signed the MOU in the 
second half of the financial year 2009-10 and submitted their proposal thereafter. As a 
result, only Rs.3.00 crore could be released by the Ministry by the end of January, 2010. 
As per the latest information furnished by the Ministry, central share of Grant-in-aid of 

Rs.33.31 crore to 14 States for implementation of the Scheme and Rs.9.33 crore to the 
Childline India Foundation, Mumbai for running the Childline service in the country has 
been released.  
 
6.4 The Committee notes that against a projected requirement of Rs.400 crore, Rs.300 
crore has been allocated for the Scheme in 2010-11 mainly for  the setting up of Juvenile 
Justice Board and Child Welfare  Committee, Special Juvenile Police  Units, Child   
Protection Societies  and Open  Shelters, Child Line Service in 163 cities in the country  
for 300 districts of 25 States/UTs.  The Committee appreciates the lofty targets set for 
the implementation of the Scheme.  Howeve r, getting the remaining States/UTs to 
sign the MOU specially due to the Scheme being on a cost sharing basis and setting 
up of Juvenile Justice Board, Child Welf are Committees, Special Juvenile Police 
Units, Child Protection Services in 300 distri cts of at least 25 States would not be an 
easy task.  Besides that, implementation of  the Scheme in the 17 States which have 
signed the MoU will also have to be closel y monitored, so as to tackle the initial 
problem areas. The Committee hopes that the assurance of the Ministry with regard 
to the speedy and accelerated implementation of the scheme holds true.

6.6 Committee's attention has been drawn by the  Model Rules framed under the 
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 which provide for 
constitution of Inspection Committees by the State Governments/UTs at State, District or 
City Level.  These Committees are required to visit and oversee the conditions of the 
institutions/homes  and appropriateness of the processes for safety, well being, review the 
standards of care and protection, look into the functioning of the Management Committee 
and Children’s Committee and give suggestions for improvement.  The Committee  
finds that these Committees are being se t up by the respective State Governments 

under ICPS. The Committee apprehends that so far this very important monitoring 
mechanism envisaged under the Juvenile Ju stice (Care and Protection of Children) 
Act, 2000 was not there in position or not effective, if existing in majority of the 
States. The Committee strongly feels that in  the absence of constant and rigorous 
monitoring, the very objective of all such homes, i.e., protection of vulnerable 
children would remain on paper inspite of  lofty schemes and substantive funding. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Centre has to play a pro-active role 
in getting the monitoring mechanism of Inspection Committee and activated in the 
real sense. The Committee wo uld appreciate if publicity to services provided by 
these Child Lines is given in the cities fr om where these are operating on a regular 
basis through both print and electronic media.  
 
6.7 An important component of the Scheme is Child Line Services which provides 
services for children in emergency situations.  During the year 2009-10 (till December, 
2009), child line had received 16 lakh calls  out of which about 10 lakh calls were 
silent/blank/wrong/crank/fun/abusive and phon e testing calls. Remaining calls were for 
medical help, shelter, rescue, repatriation, information and referral services, help in child 
tracking etc. However, even if life of one child is saved through this Help Line, it can be 
said that the very purpose for setting up such Help Line has been served. At present, this 
facility is available in only 83 cities of the country. 163 citites are proposed to be covered 
during 2010-11. 
 
6.8 Attention of the Committee has been draw n to the plight of children of sex 
workers, child labourers and child beggars.  It has been observed that these children 

are a vulnerable lot without proper housing, food and schooling.  Rehabilitation of 
such children becomes important.  The Committee is of the view that special 
provisions and reservations should be made for including these children in the list of 
beneficiaries of the Integrated Child Pr otection Scheme. While welcoming this 
proposed expansion, the Committee would like to point out that ideal position would 
be when his facility is made available across the country. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that concerted efforts may be made by the Ministry in persuading all 
the State Governments to give maximum coverage to Child Line Services.

under the new Scheme, endeavour would be to  streamline the process of scrutiny and 
approvals so that the time-lag between the receipt of applications and their 
approval/rejection is cut down significantl y. The Committee would also like to point 
out that a mechanism whereby both surprise  and regular inspections of functional 

hostels are carried out, needs to be evolve d. This would ensure that the Scheme is

7.7 The Committee would like to draw th e attention of the Ministry towards 
areas where there are numerous industries forming an industrial hub but there are no

such areas which offer ample employment opportunities to them.  Further, only 887 
hostels sanctioned do not cater to the ne eds  of all the working women across the 
country.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that additional hostels for working 
women should be sanctioned especially in areas left uncovered so that more and more 
number of women are benefitted from the scheme. 
 
VIII. CENTRAL ADOPTION RESOURCE AGENCY (CARA) 
8.1 The Central Adoption Resource Agency (CARA) is an Autonomous Body under 
the Ministry of Women and Child Development.  It is the central authority in the country to 
deal with adoption matters as per the Hague Convention on Protection of Children and 
Cooperation in respect of inter-country adoption ratified by Government of India in 2003.  
It is fully funded by the Government of India.  Its mandate is to find a loving and caring 
family for every orphan/destitute/surrendered child in the country.  While CARA is 
engaged in clearing inter-country adoption of Indian children, one of its major tasks is to 
promote in-country adoption.  In fact, CARA ensures that no Indian child is given for inter-
country adoption without him/her having been considered by Indian families residing in 
India.  CARA also provides financial assi stance to various NGOs and Government run 
Homes to promote quality child care to such children and place them in domestic adoption.

meagre allocation for the scheme was under-utilized as indicated below :-

X. CONDENSED COURSES OF EDUCATION FOR WOMEN  
10.1 The Scheme of Condensed Courses of Education was initiated by CSWB in 1958 
to cater to the needs of adult girls/women who could not join mainstream education 
system or who were drop-outs from formal schools.  The scheme aims to provide 
educational opportunities to girls/women above the age of 15 years along with additional 
inputs of skill-development/vocational training.  The main focus of the scheme is to 
ensure that contents of the course are need-based and modified according to local 
requirement. 
10.2 During 2009-10, as on 31
st January, 2010, expenditure reported was Rs. 4.72 
crore against an allocation of Rs. 7.00 crores.  Committee has been given to understand 
that  during 2009-10 because of less than required fund allocation, only past liabilities 
were cleared.  As a result, against a target of 800 courses to be conducted during 2009-
10, only one course could be conducted.  The Committee wonders whether this 
utilization is towards clearanc e of past liabilities only an d would like to be apprised 
of the number of beneficiaries in 2009-10.  The Committee  would like to draw the 
attention of the Ministry to wards the utilization status  of allocated funds during 
2007-2008 and 2008-09.  Against a provision of Rs. 14.00 crore during these two 
years, funds amounting to only Rs. 7.60 crore could be utilized.  The Committee is, 
therefore, not fully convinced by the clarif ication given by the Ministry for targeted 
beneficiaries not being covered during 2009-10. The Committee is of the view that 
funds should be fully utilized in an op timum and judicious manner and set targets 
should be achieved within the specified time period. 
 

10.3 Rs. 9.00 crore has been allocated for the scheme in 2010-11.  The Committee has 
been given to understand that 800 courses @ approximately Rs. 1.00 lakh per course 
would be conducted in the year 2010-11 which would benefit 20,000 women.  In addition 
to this, approximately Rs. 2.00 crore will be required to clear past liabilities for the year 
2007-08 and 2008-09 as two year courses started during 2008 and 2009 will be 
completed in 2010-11.  Balance of 25 per cent  grants is to be reimbursed after settlement 
of accounts.  The Committee hopes that this allo cation would be fully utilized and 
800 courses would be conducted during 2010- 11.  It also hopes that unlike 2009-10, 
this financial year would not just witnes s the clearance of past liabilities.  The 
Committee finds monitoring of the scheme is  being done both by State Boards and 
CSWB.  The Committee would like to have a Status Report on the NGOs not 
performing well during the last three years identified by the Monitoring Officers 
along with follow-up action (State-wise)  The Committee has been given to 
understand that on an average 50 per cent beneficiaries under the Scheme are being 
provided placement.  The Committee would li ke to have an idea about the States 
showing good results in this vital component of the scheme.  
 
XI. SCHEME FOR RELIEF TO AND REHABILITATION OF RAPE 
VICTIMS 
 
 
11.1 The Scheme for Relief to and Rehabilita tion of Rape Victims envisages providing 
interim relief to victims of rape on finding of prima facie case of rape as well as expenses 
for rehabilitation and other support services, including medical treatment, counseling and 
vocational training. The Scheme envisages establishment of Criminal Injuries 
Compensation Boards at the Central, State and District levels for its effective 

implementation. Recognizing the need for speedy disposal of applications, the scheme 
proposes to lay down the time limit within which the relief would be available to the 
victim. 
 
11.2 The scheme has been under formulation for the last few years.  As a result, token 
allocation of Rs. 1.00 crore was made in 2006-07 and 2007-08.  Thereafter, although 
substantive provision of Rs. 40.00 crore and Rs. 59.00 crore has been made in 2008-09 
and 2009-10  respectively,  it has remained unspent.   Considering the number of rape 
cases reported every year, the Ministry had estimated an annual requirement of Rs. 254 
crore approximately to launch the scheme. On a specific query in this regard, the 
Committee has been informed that consultations with various Stake-holders have been 
held on the draft scheme prepared by the National Commission for Women.  A National 
Consultation on the Scheme has also been held on 7
th March, 2010.  Based on the 
recommendations received in the National Consultation, the Ministry is at present in the 
process of finalization of the scheme .  The Committee would like to point out that 
considerable time has already been taken in the formulation of the scheme.  Almost 
one plan period has been taken for this exercise.  The Committee apprehends that  
formal approval of the scheme from competent authority will also have to undergo a 
number of stages which again is a protracted exercise.  The Committee, therefore, 
would like to impress upon the Ministry  to make all conceivable efforts for 
expeditions completion of all the preparatory activities so as to ensure the launch of 
this much-required scheme by the end of the Eleventh Plan.   
 

11.3 The Committee observes that provision of Rs. 40.00 crore has been kept for 2010-
11 which is meant for providing   interim reli ef to 15,000 victims and medical relief to 
2500 victims. The Committee feels that a beginning has to be made for launch of this 
scheme even if at a small scale.  In the meantime, the Ministry has to make all out 
efforts for getting the funds as required under the scheme.   The Committee also 
recommends to the Ministry for working out a set of guidelines for ascertaining 
whether the cases brought forward are ge nuine and assistance is provided to the 
victims as envisaged under the scheme. 
 
XIII. NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR WOMEN (NCW)  
12.1 The National Commission for Women (NCW) set up in 1992 is a statutory apex 
national level body under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.  NCW 
reviews the provisions relating to the safeguards for women under the Constitution as 
well as in other laws.  It takes up petitions from women for redressal of their grievances, 
and does promotional research for the advancement of women, takes suo moto notice of 
matters relating to deprivation of women’s rights etc.  and takes up the issues with 
appropriate authorities. 
 
12.2 The Committee is aware that the National Commission for Women is the 
only  national level authority having the mandate of protecting the rights of women 
across the country.   The most crucial task assigned to the Commission is to 
investigate specific problems or situations arising out of discrimination/atrocities 
against women.  However, the Commit tee feels that the Commission has not 
succeeded fully in carrying out this mandate.  This is borne out by the status of 

complaints received by the Commission.  As per the information made available to 
the Committee, out of 15,854 complaints  registered with the Commission during 
2007-08 and 12,895 complaints during 2008-09, 1781 and 1166 complaints are 
pending respectively.   The Committee finds  the details of complaints on which 
Action Taken Reports from concerned authorities are still pending as more 
disturbing.  Out of 8640 and 7509 complaints registered in 2007-08 and 2008-09 
respectively, ATRs, are pending on 5610 and 4679 complaints respectively.  This 
clearly shows that the matter has not pr oceeded beyond the complaint registered 
with the Commission and sent to the conc erned authorities for necessary action.  
Therefore, it would not be wrong to conclude that no relief whatsoever has been 
provided to the victim in such a case.  The very fact that a very large number of 
complaints from 2007-08 and 2008-09 conti nue to remain pending defeats the very 
purpose of mandate of safeguarding the ri ghts and interests of women folk of the 
country, with which the Commission has been entrusted.  The Committee can well 
imagine the fate of 13,696 complaints registered with NCW (as on 31.01.2010) 
during 2009-10.   The Committee strongly feels that the National Commission for 
Women needs to be empowered so  as to be in a position to take conclusive action in 
cases relating to redressal of grievances received from victims.    
 
12.3 Another very important mandate of NCW is to review the provisions relating to 
safeguards for women under the Constitution as well as in other laws, and recommend 
suitable amendments as and when required.  Committee’s attention has been drawn to a 
seminar on the Immoral Traffic Prevention Act, 1956 conducted by the National Law 
School.  It was suggested that a Central Anti-Trafficking Nodal Authority on the lines of 

Narcotics Control Bureau needs to be set up.  Nobody can deny the fact that the problem 
of exploitation of young girls specially from remote and tribal areas has become very 
serious and needs to be tackled effectively.  The Committee therefore, strongly feels 
that the National Commission for Women has to play a proactive role in such 
matters.     
 
XIII. MERGER OF SCHEME OF SWADHAR AND SHORT STAY HOME 
13.1 The Scheme of Swadhar was introduced in 2001-02 with the objective of 
addressing the requirements of women in difficult circumstances.  It is a shelter-based 
scheme for providing relief and rehabilitatio n to women in difficult circumstances.  It 
seeks to rehabilitate widows, victims of tr afficking, victims of natural calamities, 
mentally challenged and destitute women.  The scheme provides for support like food, 
skill development, legal support, medical faciliti es helpline service etc.  At present, there 
are 317 Homes and 237 help-lines are functional under the Scheme. 
 
13.2 The Scheme of Short Stay Homes seeks to protect and rehabilitate women and 
girls who are facing social ostracism, exploitation or other causes.  The Scheme provides 
services like medical care, skill developm ent training, education, vocational and 
rehabilitation services and re-adjustments in  family/society.  The Ministry has also 
anchored help-line services for women in distress in some Short Stay Homes.  There are 
414 Homes and 30 new Homes are anticipated for sanction during 2010-11 
 
13.3 The Committee has been informed that these two schemes would be merged.  The 
Ministry proposes to launch a new scheme to replace the existing two schemes during the 
year 2010-11.  The merged scheme is expected to provide a network of shelter homes all 

over the country to take care of the needs of one of the most marginalized and vulnerable 
sections of the society i.e. women without family or societal support and independent 
means of income.  The scheme is still unde r formulation and the Ministry is making 
efforts to provide enhanced financial norms for every component, emphasizing on 
generation of livelihood options through vocational training, simplify application 
procedures and putting in place a stricter monitoring regime. During the transition of 
switching from the two schemes to one scheme, each home under the existing schemes 
shall be reviewed with respect to its performance, need assessment  of the number of 
homes in an area vis-à-vis the existing number, ability and willingness of the 
implementing organizations to comply with the revised criteria and other relevant factors. 
 
13.4 The Committee is of the view that the merger of these two schemes with 
almost similar objectives is a step in the right direction.  However, many aspects like 
financial norms, new compon ents, monitoring mechanism etc. would need to be 
taken into consideration for the implem entation of the me rged scheme The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry evalua tes all  aspects of both the schemes 
carefully before its implementation.  The Committee is doubtful about the 
implementation of the merged scheme in the year 2010-11.  The Committee also 
wonders by when the process of signing of  MOUs  with State Governments will be 
undertaken.  The Committee can only hope th at the new scheme  will be finalized at 
the earliest and all formalities will be  completed and approvals obtained so that 
there is no undue delay in the implementati on of this merged scheme which is the 
only support for many marginalized women in the country.

XV. CONCLUSION 
15. The Committee while reviewing the allocation, utilization trends and 
performance of various schemes administered by the Ministry, finds that utilization 
of allocated funds has been mo re or less satisfactory.  The Ministry, however, needs 
to monitor the implementation of scheme s as many schemes could not accomplish 
their set targets, with special focus on the implementing agencies like the NGOs.  
The target group of the schemes of the Mi nistry are women and children and they 
are the most vulnerable section of our soci ety and they need to be addressed with 
utmost care and sensitivity.   The Ministry needs to lay emphasis on the timely 
implementation of its new schemes and the revamping of the schemes under process.  
The Committee believes that concerted effo rts of the Ministry would certainly lead 
to the evolution of an efficient delivery mechanism with minimum hindrances.  

OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE 
 
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
While appreciating the genuine require ments and track-record of optimum 
utilization of funds in well-established schemes like ICDS, the Committee would like 
to point out that with respect to schemes yet to be approved, the Ministry has to 
primarily focus on getting the schemes ap proved expeditiously by the competent  
authority.                                                                                                              (Para 2.3)  
 
The Committee takes note of a positive development with regard to women-
specific schemes.  So far trend of allocation for these schemes has been at a low level.  
However, allocation of Rs. 1691.00 crore for women-specific schemes in 2010-11 
shows an increase of almost five times when compared with provision of Rs. 349.00 
crore for 2009-10.   However, the Committee has a word of caution.  This 
tremendous enhancement in allocation has to be matched by optimum utilization 
also.  The Committee has observed that during 2009-10 also, like the previous  
years, funds allocated for majority of th e women-specific schemes have remained 
under-utilized inspite of being reduced at the RE stage.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that all required steps be ta ken for optimum and j udicious utilization 
of allocated funds for women-specific schemes.                                               (Para 2.4) 
 
A disturbing trend noticed by the Committee is undue delay in the final 
approval of a new scheme.  The Committee has been drawing the attention of the 
Ministry in this regard for the last few years.  However, no corrective measures 
seem to have been initiated by the Ministry  so far.  As a result, new schemes with 
ambitious vision continue to remain in th e formulation stage for years.  The only 
redeeming feature is allocation of funds  without break with utilization status 
remaining nil at the end of the year.  Year 2009-10 was also no exception as schemes 
like Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for empowerment of Adoloscent Girls, Relief to and 
Rehabilitation of Rape victims, etc are still under formulation or approval stage.   

The Committee would also like to point out that the Scheme for Relief to and 
Rehabilitation of Rape Victims has continue d to remain on pap er for the last four 
years with token provision of Rs. 1.00 crore starting from 2006-07 and substantive 
provision (Rs. 40.00 crore) being made in 2008-09.  The Committee finds that 
extension of an existing sc heme also entails a long process.  Second phase of 
Swayamsidha Scheme is to be  started.  However, from  2008-09 onwards, allocated 
funds have remained unutilized, as the scheme is yet to be approved.          (Para 2.6) 
 
The Committee expresses its grave co ncern over under-utilization of funds 
which are meant for the benefit of the peop le of North-East who face geographical 
as well as climatic adversities.  The Committee believes that assiduous efforts should 
be made to utilize the funds in a more  effective and judicious manner and the 
matter of under-utilization of allocated funds should be taken up with the concerned 
States.                                                                                                                   (Para 2.7) 
                                                                                                                                
The Committee has time a nd again emphasized on liquidating the pendency 
of large number of UCs involving huge su ms of funds.  Monitoring of UCs by 
comprehensive web-based software called the ‘UC Package’, repeated reminders 
and other measures on the part of the Ministry have not proved to be very 
successful as evident from the above.  The Committee was informed that majority of 
pending UCs were mostly ve ry old cases involving small amount and no fresh 
proposals from such NGOs were under th e consideration of the Ministry.  The 
Committee strongly feels that it would have  been appropriate if pendency of very 
old cases was liquidated without any further delay within the financial norms.  The 
Committee is, however, surprised to note th at the year-wise details furnished by the 
Ministry depict an entirely different posi tion.  Number of 5888 pending UCs date 
back to 1986-87.  What is more disturbing is that out of 5888 pending UCs 
amounting to Rs. 345.38 crore, as many as 4096 UCs amounting to Rs. 142.29 crore 
relate to the period from 1986-87 to 1999-2000.  The Committee takes a serious view 
of this misleading information furnished to it earlier.  The Committee reiterates the 
importance of pro-active role of the Ministry with active co-operation of the State 
Governments and other agencie s involved in the implemen tation of the schemes of 

the Ministry.   The Committee would also like to point out that the very fact that 
UCs are outstanding for long periods indicates that there are inherent  constraints 
in the implementation of schemes.  No n-releasing further grants to NGOs till 
submission of pending UCs is as per the financial norms.  However, one must not 
forget that the main objective of outreach of the scheme to the targeted beneficiaries 
also gets diluted in the process.  The Commi ttee, therefore, strongly feels that it is 
high time for the Ministry to identify th e root causes of pendency of UCs and take 
steps for removal of the same.                                                                            (Para 2.8) 
 
The Committee in its previous Report had highlighted the issue of unspent 
balances with State Governments and ha d recommended that the matter of unspent 
balances should be urgently taken up with the concerned State Governments so that 
the implementation of an important scheme like ICDS is not hampered.  The 
Ministry has to constantly monitor specially in view of substantive enhancement of 
funds for ICDS.                                                                                                   (Para 2.9) 
  
  The Committee would also appreciate if all steps are taken to ensure non-
involvement of defaulter NGOs identified during the implementation of Phase 1 of 
Swayamsidha.  The Ministry should also vigorously pursue with the respective 
States/UTs the matter of  refunding of unspent balances through RBI, Nagpur. 
                                                                                                                             (Para 2.10)

those not performing well.                                                                                  (Para 3.1) 
 
Funding For ICDS

   The Committee notes that all the states/UTs have been sensitized to take all 
the required administrative measures for immediate operationalisation of all the

Pre-School Education Kits  
 
   The Committee is very disappointed with this state of affairs.  It seems that 
States are not interested in procuring the Pre-school Education Kits for their 
Children.  The Committee would like to point out that these kits are a replacement 
for pre-parental education in nursery school .  They can be considered an important 
tool for enhancing literacy at  the end of class V.  World- wide, it is an established 
fact that children having a certain minimum vocabulary before entering school have 
a higher chance of achieving literacy at the end of class V.   The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that concerted efforts need to be made so as to convince the 
States to include this very crucial component financial assistance for which is 
provided by the Centre.                                                                                   (Para 3.4.2)

 While appreciating the efforts of the Ministry, the Committee would like to 
draw its attention to the fact that the Report of the Thirteenth Finance Commission

Manpower Under ICDS

IV. RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL CRECHE SCHEME FOR THE CHILDREN 
OF WORKING MOTHERS. 
 
On a review of the achievement level of the physical targets under the 
scheme, the Committee notes that outreach of  this scheme has shown no expansion. 
Number of crèches and coverage of children have remained at the same level.  The 
Committee has been persistently advocating for expansion of this scheme which is 
primarily meant to take care of children of working mothers with meagre income. 
The Committee is disturbed to note that instead of increasing, the coverage of this 
scheme has started showing a downward trend. The Committee finds that during 
2009-10, against a target of 31,718 crèches, only 26,177 crèches could be opened up 
to 31 st December, 2009. As a result, number of  child beneficiaries also stood at 
6,54,425 against a target of 7,92,950 children.                                                  (Para 4.2) 
 
The Committee is of the view that deficiencies like improper maintenance of 
records and registers, non-provision of  supplementary nutrition, unsatisfactory 
coverage of children, irregular payment of honorarium to crèche workers, doctors 
not visiting the crèches regularly noticed by the monitoring agencies in the crèches 
being run by BAJSS are of a very seriou s nature. The Committee finds that inquiry 
into complaints against the NGO is yet to be completed by the Vigilance Wing of the 
Ministry. The Committee is of the firm opinion that the inquiry should be completed 
at the earliest, followed by action against all the concerned agencies/authorities.      
                                                                                                                             (Para 4.3) 
 
The Committee finds that charge of 5522 crèches being run by BAJSS was 
temporarily transferred to CSWB on 18th November, 2008. It has been more that 16 
months since then and CSWB which is alrea dy handling 20,893 crèches continues to 
have the additional charge of 5522 crèches. The Committee wonders whether the 

CSWB has the required manpower to effectively handle the additional 
responsibility. The Committee is somewhat su rprised to note that as per the Annual 
Action Plan 2010-11, around 26,000 creches  benefitting 4,12,875 children are 
targeted to be covered. This target shows a considerable decline when compared 
with achievement of 26,177 crèches with coverage of 6,54,425 children as on 31 st 
December, 2009. This confirms Committe e’s apprehensions about 5522 crèches 
earlier run by BAJSS being non-functional. No other plausible reason seems to be 
there for such a situation. The Committee would like to be apprised about the status 
of all the functional crèches.                                                                              (Para 4.4) 
 
The Committee notes that NIPCCD which was requested to prepare a 
Concept Paper suggesting revision in the existing scheme with a view to restructure 
the scheme, has submitted the paper on 2 nd February, 2010. At present, an internal 
Committee of the Ministry is examining the Report. The Committee notes that the 
Concept Paper has recomme nded major changes in the cost norms, manpower 
requirement, inclusion of new components like Play and Sleeping Material Kit (PSE 
Kit), rent for crèche building, extensive tr aining for the worker s and monitoring on 
six monthly basis.  The Committee welcomes these suggestions for improvement 
which were long awaited. The Committee wo uld appreciate if the final decision on 
the Concept Paper is taken at the earliest and approval process is also expedited. 
The Committee notices a major change suggested in the Concept Paper in the 
implementing agencies from CSWB a nd two NGOs to SHGs, Mahila Mandals, 
Women’s’ Organizations, Panchayats a nd Tribal Associations etc. under the 
supervision of the State Governments. The Co mmittee feels that this is a step in the 
right direction.                                                                                                     (Para 4.5)

hopes that during 2010-11, substantive nu mber of such Homes/Shelters will be 
covered under the Scheme.                                                                                 (Para 6.5) 
 
   The Committee finds that the Inspection Committees are being set up by the 
respective State Governments under ICPS. The Committee apprehends that so far 

this very important monito ring mechanism envisaged under the Juvenile Justice 
(Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 was not there in position or not 
effective, if existing in majority of the States. The Committee strongly feels that in 
the absence of constant and rigorous monitoring, the very objective of all such 
homes, i.e., protection of vulnerable childr en would remain on paper inspite of lofty 
schemes and substantive fundi ng. The Committee, therefor e, recommends that the 
Centre has to play a pro-active role in getting the monitoring mechanism of 
Inspection Committee and activated in the real sense. The Committee would 
appreciate if publicity to services provided by these Child Lines is given in the cities 
from where these are operating on a regular basis through both print and electronic 
media.                                                                                                                   (Para 6.6) 
 
Attention of the Committee has been draw n to the plight of children of sex 
workers, child labourers and child beggars.  It has been observed that these children 
are a vulnerable lot without proper housing, food and schooling.  Rehabilitation of 
such children becomes important.  The Committee is of the view that special 
provisions and reservations should be made for including these children in the list of 
beneficiaries of the Integrated Child Pr otection Scheme. While welcoming this 
proposed expansion, the Committee would like to point out that ideal position would 
be when his facility is made available across the country. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that concerted efforts may be made by the Ministry in persuading all 
the State Governments to give maximum coverage to Child Line Services.  
                                                                                                                   (Para 6.8) 
 
VII. SCHEME OF HOSTELS FOR WORKING WOMEN 
 
 
  The Committee has been given to understand that Ministry has started a case 
by case review of all incomplete projects and has advised the State Governments in 
13 cases to recover the amount of grant di sbursed  along with prescribed interest 
failing which they have been advised to take over the premises for use of any activity 
related to welfare of  women and children.  The Committee is satisfied with the pro-
active action initiated by the Ministry against the defaulting organizations. The 

Committee recommends that action against al l defaulting organizations should be 
initiated.  Efforts should be made to complete the incomplete projects so that the 
objective of the scheme is not defeated.                                                             (Para 7.4) 
   
The Committee is of the view that three years of the Eleventh Plan are 
already over and the process of revision of the Scheme still remains incomplete. 
Concerted efforts have to be made to overcome procedural difficulties and 
ambiguities. The Committee hopes that with new components of maintenance grants, 
grant for hostels in rented buildings, accre ditation of PG like accommodation, grant 
for initial furnishing etc., the revamped Sc hemed will go a long way in reaching the 
targetted beneficiaries in the real sense. Th e Committee is also happy to note that 
under the new Scheme, endeavour would be to  streamline the process of scrutiny and 
approvals so that the time-lag between the receipt of applications and their 
approval/rejection is cut down significantl y. The Committee would also like to point 
out that a mechanism whereby both surprise  and regular inspections of functional 
hostels are carried out, needs to be evolve d. This would ensure that the Scheme is 
benefitting the targetted beneficiaries.                                                                 (Para 7.6) 
 
The Committee would like to draw th e attention of the Ministry towards 
areas where there are numerous industries forming an industrial hub but there are no 
provision of hostels for work ing women due to which women do not opt to work in 
such areas which offer ample employment opportunities to them.  Further, only 887 
hostels sanctioned do not cater to the needs of all the working women across the 
country.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that additional hostels for working 
women should be sanctioned especially in areas left uncovered so that more and more 
number of women are benefitted from the scheme.                                            (Para 7.7) 
 
VIII. CENTRAL ADOPTION RESOURCE AGENCY (CARA) 
 
The Committee was given to understand that the budget for the years 2008-
09 and 2009-10 could not be utilized due to human resource deficit in the 
organization.  Moreover, the Action Plan for the year 2009-10 was approved by the 

Management Committee of CARA only in th e month of January, 2010 because it was 
not in place since April, 2009.  Hence, no activities could be carried out prior to 
January, 2010.  The Committee has been informed that the post of Secretary, CARA 
has been filled on a regular basis after almost five years. The Committee is not 
convinced with the justification given by the Ministry.   The Committee expresses its 
doubt whether CARA would be able to fu lfill its obligations in view of human 
resource deficit in the organization. The Committee also finds the allocation for 
CARA inadequate for carrying out a number of functions and therefore recommends 
for increase in allocation for the organization.                                                    (Para 8.2) 
 
The Committee would like to know the reasons for reductions in number of 
adoptions over the last three years.  The Committee observes that such a state of 
affairs was probably due to human resource deficit in CARA and delay in 
finalization of Action Plan of 2009-10 and its inability to carry out its most 
important function i.e. of facilitating adoptions.  The Committee hopes that with the 
post of Secretary being filled up and the Action Plan ready for the year 2010-11, 
CARA would be able to utilize the allo cated funds and the year 2010-11 would 
witness an increase of inter-country and in-country adoptions.                     (Para 8.3) 
 
The Committee  hopes that the hindrances faced by CARA at present in 
cases of inter-country adoption like judicial delays, clearances from CWC declaring 
children legally free for adoption and ille gal adoption/direct adoption will be taken 
care of in the revamped scheme.                                                                        (Para 8.4) 
 
VIII. RASTHTRIYA MAHILA KOSH (RMK) 
 
The Committee appreciates the initiative of the Government regarding 
restructuring RMK so that its corpus is ra ised to Rs. 500 crore which is likely to 
benefit many more poor women who woul d be able to earn their living by 
themselves.  The Committee would like to be  a p p r i s e d  a s  t o  w h e n  t h i s  p r o c e s s  o f  
restructuring would be comple te and what new components more beneficial for the 

targeted beneficiaries (like the rate of in terest at which the loan would be given 
would be included in the restructured RMK.                                                   (Para 9.3) 
 
In view of restructuring of RMK, the Committee would like to point out that 
the need of the hour is to focus on better management of the portfolio of the poor 
women and improving the overall chain which converts the viable ones into genuine 
women entrepreneurs.  Micro-finance organizations should identify the needs of the 
poor women, their saving capacity and time  period and mode of repayment of loan.  
It is time to explore more about the whole philosophy of micro financing and 
successful experiences in the international context.                                         (Para 9.4) 
 
As per the details furnished by the Ministry, out of Rs. 30.30  crore 
sanctioned in 2008-09, Rs. 26.47 crore was disbursed to Rs. 36, 166 beneficiaries.  
Similarly, during 2009-10, against a sanctioned amount of Rs. 9.01 crore, Rs. 11.91 
crore were disbursed, number of beneficiaries being only 9904.  State-wise details 
indicate that during these two years, ther e are States where funds were sanctioned 
but there were no disburseme nts inspite of beneficiaries reported.  There are also 
States where no sanction was there but  disbursements were duly made with no 
details of beneficiaries.  It seems that exact figures of beneficiaries during 2008-09 
and 2009-10 inspite of disbursement of loan s have not reached the Ministry so far.   
The Committee apprehends that position about the  previous years may also be on 
the same lines.  The Committee would like to have full details about funds 
sanctioned, loan disbursed, number of beneficiaries, number of implementing 
agencies involved, non-disbursed amount available with the NGOs at the beginning 
of the years for the last three years (State -wise).  The Committee would also like to 
understand in which States reach of RMK is not evident so far.                   (Para 9.5)  
 
The Committee believes that there should be  a stipulated time frame for completing 
the proceedings against these erring NGOs.  Also, strict monitoring of the NGOs 
should be an important comp onent for the real assessment of the performance level 
of the scheme.  The Ministry is contemplating to adopt the system of on-line 
monitoring of the projects sanctioned .  The Committee believes that on-line 

monitoring of the projects would help in bringing about transparency in the whole 
process and detailed information about disbursements, releases to NGOs, utilization 
figures, number of beneficiaries etc. sh ould be updated on the website of the 
Ministry at regular intervals.  Simultaneously, keeping in view the blacklisting of a 
large number of NGOs, the Committee is of the view that a viable mechanism of 
inspections (both regular and surprise) at periodic intervals involving both States 
authorities and officers from the Ministry  needs to be evolved.  Local community, 
PRIs etc. can also be involved in this exercise.                                                 (Para 9.6) 
 
IX. CONDENSED COURSES OF EDUCATION FOR WOMEN 
  
The Committee wonders whether this utilization is towards clearance of past 
liabilities only and would like to be apprised of the number of beneficiaries in 2009-
10.  The Committee would like to draw the attention of the Ministry towards the 
utilization status of allocated funds during 2007-2008 and 2008-09.  Against a 
provision of Rs. 14.00 crore during these two years, funds amounting to only Rs. 
7.60 crore could be utilized.  The Committee is, therefore, not fully convinced by the 
clarification given by the Ministry for targeted beneficiaries not being covered 
during 2009-10. The Committee is of the view that funds should be fully utilized in 
an optimum and judicious manner and set ta rgets should be achieved within the 
specified time period.                                                                                        (Para 10.2) 
 
The Committee hopes that this alloca tion would be fully utilized and 800 
courses would be conducted during 2010-11.  It also hopes that unlike 2009-10, this 
financial year would not just witness th e clearance of past liabilities.  The 
Committee finds monitoring of the scheme is  being done both by State Boards and 
CSWB.  The Committee would like to have a Status Report on the NGOs not 
performing well during the last three years identified by the Monitoring Officers 
along with follow-up action (State-wise)  The Committee has been given to 
understand that on an average 50 per cent beneficiaries under the Scheme are being 
provided placement.  The Committee would li ke to have an idea about the States 
showing good results in this vital component of the school.                          (Para 10.3) 

 
XI. SCHEME FOR RELIEF TO AND REHABILITATION OF RAPE 
VICTIMS 
 
 
The Committee would like to point out that considerable time has already 
been taken in the formulation of the scheme.  Almost one plan period has been 
taken for this exercise.  The Committee apprehends that  formal approval of the 
scheme from competent authority will al so have to undergo a number of stages 
which again is a protracted exercise.  The Committee, therefore, would like to 
impress upon the Ministry to make a ll conceivable efforts for expeditions 
completion of all the preparatory activities so as to ensure the launch of this much-
required scheme by the end of the Eleventh Plan.                                         (Para 11.2)   
 
The Committee feels that a beginning has to be made for launch of this 
scheme even if at a small scale.  In the meantime, the Ministry has to make all out 
efforts for getting the funds as required under the scheme.   The Committee also 
recommends to the Ministry for working out a set of guidelines for ascertaining 
whether the cases brought forward are ge nuine and assistance is provided to the 
victims as envisaged under the scheme.                                                          (Para 11.3) 
 
XIII. NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR WOMEN (NCW)  
 
The Committee is aware that the National Commission for Women is the 
only national level authority having the mandate of protecting the rights of women 
across the country.   The most crucial task assigned to the Commission is to 
investigate specific problems or situations arising out of discrimination/atrocities 
against women.  However, the Commit tee feels that the Commission has not 
succeeded fully in carrying out this mandate.  This is borne out by the status of 
complaints received by the Commission.  As per the information made available to 
the Committee, out of 15,854 complaints  registered with the Commission during 
2007-08 and 12,895 complaints during 2008-09, 1781 and 1166 complaints are 
pending respectively.   The Committee finds  the details of complaints on which 
Action Taken Reports from concerned authorities are still pending as more 

disturbing.  Out of 8640 and 7509 complaints registered in 2007-08 and 2008-09 
respectively, ATRs, are pending on 5610 and 4679 complaints respectively.  This 
clearly shows that the matter has not pr oceeded beyond the complaint registered 
with the Commission and sent to the conc erned authorities for necessary action.  
Therefore, it would not be wrong to conclude that no relief whatsoever has been 
provided to the victim in such a case.  The very fact that a very large number of 
complaints from 2007-08 and 2008-09 conti nue to remain pending defeats the very 
purpose of mandate of safeguarding the ri ghts and interests of women folk of the 
country, with which the Commission has been entrusted.  The Committee can well 
imagine the fate of 13,696 complaints registered with NCW (as on 31.01.2010) 
during 2009-10.   The Committee strongly feels that the National Commission for 
Women needs to be empowered so  as to be in a position to take conclusive action in 
cases relating to redressal of grievances received from victims.                   (Para 12.2) 
   
   The Committee therefore, strongly feels that the National Commission for 
Women has to play a proactive role in such matters.                                    (Para 12.3)  
 
XIII. MERGER OF SCHEME OF SWADHAR AND SHORT STAY HOME 
 
The Committee is of the view that the merger of these two schemes with 
almost similar objectives is a step in the right direction.  However, many aspects like 
financial norms, new compon ents, monitoring mechanism etc. would need to be 
taken into consideration for the implem entation of the me rged scheme The 
Committee hopes that the Ministry evaluates all aspects of both the schemes 
carefully before its implementation.  The Committee is doubtful about the 
implementation of the merged scheme in the year 2010-11.  The Committee also 
wonders by when the process of signing of  MOUs  with State Governments will be 
undertaken.  The Committee can only hope th at the new scheme  will be finalized at 
the earliest and all formalities will be  completed and approvals obtained so that 
there is no undue delay in the implementati on of this merged scheme which is the 
only support for many marginalized women in the country.                        (Para 13.4) 
 

XIV. COMPREHENSIVE SCHEME FOR COMBATING TRAFFICKING 
(UJJAWALA) 
 
The Committee is unhappy over under-utilization of funds for this scheme 
for the last three years.  The Committee is  of the view that problem-areas in the 
implementation of the scheme should be id entified and solutions looked for.  The 
Committee believes that valuable inputs and help can be taken from NIPCCD which 
conducts orientation courses, sensitization programmes etc. with respect to this 
scheme.  The Committee hopes that the Mi nistry would take concrete steps for 
optimum and judicious utilization of fu nds for a vital scheme like this.  The 
Committee hopes that the allocation of Rs. 10.00 crore for 2010-2011 will not remain 
under-utilized.                                                                                                             (14.2) 
The Committee finds that achievement of targets was comparatively better in  
2008-09 than in 2009-10.  In 2009-10,  against the target of 12,850, only 2800 
benefited from the scheme.  Also, against th e target of 150 (new) and 107 (existing)  
proposals for projects to be approved, only 40 (new) and 39 (existing) proposals 
were approved.                                                                                                  (Para 14.3) 
 
The Committee believes that the scheme  is the only scheme to prevent 
trafficking, rescuing and rehabilitating victims etc. This scheme should be 
implemented with a vigour as it helps in givi ng new life to the victims of trafficking. 
Concerted efforts should be made to ac hieve the targets set and benefit maximum 
number of women and children. Care shou ld be taken to handle the cases with 
utmost sensitivity and avoi d harassing of victims.  The Committee, further, 
recommends to the Ministry to set up a Spe cial Cell to monitor human trafficking, 
particularly among girls and women.  Provision for taking care of children of 
trafficked women should be made so as to give these children basic education, 
housing etc. to enable them to lead a normal life.                                          (Para 14.4) 
 
 
 
 

XV. CONCLUSION 
 
The Committee while reviewing the allocation, utilization trends and 
performance of various schemes admini stered by the Ministry, finds that 
utilization of allocated funds has been mo re or less satisfactory.  The Ministry, 
however, needs to monitor the implementation of schemes as many schemes 
could not accomplish their set targets, with special focus on the implementing 
agencies like the NGOs.  The target group of the schemes of the Ministry are 
women and children and they are the most vulnerable section of our society and 
they need to be addressed with utmost care and sensitivity.  The Ministry needs 
to lay emphasis on the timely implementation of its new schemes and the 
revamping of the schemes under process.  The Committee believes that 
concerted efforts of the Ministry would certainly lead to the evolution of an 
efficient delivery mechanism with minimum hindrances.                           
                                                                                                                    (Para 15)

REPORT

1.1 The main function of the Department of Education is to evolve educational policy
and also to coordinate and determine standards in higher education,: including research,
The Department also looks after the expansion and development of technical education to
improve the quality of text books, administrative scholarships and various other schemes/
programmes. The Department coordinates the programmes of assistance and other
activities with UNESCO. The Department mainly undertakes the Programmes relating to
elementary education, school and physical education, university and higher education, adult
education and technical education.

General Budget Allocations

1.2 The overall allocation made to the Department during 1994-95 was Rs. 1549 crores,
which was increased to Rs. 1574 crores in the revised estimates on plan side. The total
budgetary allocation for the Department for 1995-96 is Rs. 2704.07 crores, which comes to
around 1.57% of the total central budget. The Committee is distressed to note that our
country, which is having more than 90 crore population (1991 census), 47.8 percent of
which are illiterate, is sounding only such meagre portion of Central Budget on Education.
Another disturbing factor is that whereas the States contribute nearly 91% of the total
expenditure on education in the country, the Centre spends just 9%. Similarly, while the
States spend about 20% of their budget on education, on an average, the Centre spends
just 1.57%.

1.3 The Committee, while welcoming the commitment made by the Prime Minister about
achieving the norm of 6% of GDP as public expenditure on education, feels that it should
not remain a distant dream. Unless the objective is reflected in budgetary allocations, the
target is unlikely to be achieved. The Department's constant endeavour should be to reach
the goal. Towards this end, the Committee suggests that the Department should prepare a
projection paper to indicate the phased increase in allocations to achieve the set target.

1.4 The Committee notes with concern that 94% of the budget on education is spent on
salaries and only 6% is left for teaching, learning, equipment, text books, teacher training,
etc. The Secretary, Education, conceding this fact, stated that while nothing could be done
to alter the salary component. Anthing that could be added to the other components
would improve the quality of education. The Committee, however, feels that no sincere
efforts have been made in this regard. Radical steps are required to alter the scenario.

ELEMENTARY EDUCATION

2.1 Education, as a qualitative attribute of the population, is one of the most important
indicator of the socio-economic development of the country. It is a major component of
the human resource development and is thus basic to any programme of social and
economic development. There is a close relationship between literacy and other indicators
of the quality of life. The Committee notes that while the percentage of illiteracy has
declined in the country, the number of illiterates continues to grow. The Committee feels
that the root cause for illiteracy in our country is the lack of universal elementary
education, which has not been achieved, and also a very high drop out rate at the primary
stage. The Committee is happy that, on its recommendation made last year, a substantial
increase has been made in the allocation for elementary education this year. However,
there should not be any scope for complacency. The Directive Principle of State Policy
providing free and compulsory education until the age of 14 years is yet to be achieved.
Looking at the scenario of elementary education and the efforts required to be made for

2.3 The Committee notes, from the information supplied by the Department, that while
the over all rate of progress in Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) for the country as a whole has
been improving, the regional imbalances are a cause for concern. The Committee is grieved
to fined that in 9 States i.e. Bihar, Meghalaya, J&K, U.P., Goa, Manipur, Orissa, Punjab
and Rajasthan and 3 UTs, i.e. Chandigarh, Delhi, Andaman & Nicobar Islands the ratio is
considerably lower. The gross enrolment ratio at the primary stage in 1993-94 was less than
100 in many States. The position at upper primary stage is still worse. The national average
is 67.7. Except’‘Kerala, Mizoram, Himachal Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Lakshadweep and
Pondicherry, all’other States and UTs have gross enrolment ratio of less than 100.

2.4 The Committee notes that on one side we have States such as Kerala which have
achieved universal literacy as. well as Universal Elementary Education (UEE) in terms of
school participation and on the other side, we have States like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Orissa
and Madhya Pradesh where the situation is highly unsatisfactory. The Committee feels that
the efforts made so far are not sufficient to bring about the required change and to achieve
targets of universal enrolment, incorporated in the 8th Five Year Plan. The Committee
desires that steps need to be taken to increase enrolment.

Drop-outs

2.5 Drop out is one of the factors which contributes to the derailment of the Education
Policy. The Committee expresses its deep concern over the statistics relating to drop-out
rate, which was 36.32% in Classes I-V and 52.8% in Classes I-VIII in 1993-94. While
Manipur had the highest drop-out rate at primary stage (68.26%); Sikkim had the highest
rate at the upper primary stage (82.65%). Drop-out rate in Classes I-VIII was more than
70% in the States of Bihar, Manipur and Sikkim. It was between 60 to 70% in 7 States,
namely Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Karnataka, Orissa, Rajasthan and
Tripura.

2.6 The Committee feels that the issue of drop-out is a very serious problem. The
Committee observes with disappointment that the efforts made so far, particularly after the
announcement of the New Education Policy, have not yielded the desired results. In this
regard, the Committee suggests that a multi-pronged strategy be adopted and efforts should
be made for integration of various schemes with those under implementation by the
Department of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Rural Development.

Resources

2.7 The Committee feels that mobilisation of alternative resources in the elementary
education sector needs to be further strengthened. This would not only reduce the burden
on Government resources but also create an environment of responsibility and accountability
within the educational system.

Gender Disparities

2.8 The gender disparities are also conspicuous in respect of enrolment and retention. The
girls’ enrolment has grown at the primary stage from 5.4 million in 1950-51 to 46.4 million

stage are higher than those of boys. The Committee feels that the programmes implemented

Physical Education

3.38 The Committee deeply regrets that not much is being done in the field of physical
education in the schools. In fact, the Committee is surprised to learn that many States are
considering as to whether physical education should be made compulsory component of
Secondary Education or not. The Committee has noted that the Central Advisory Board of
Education appointed a sub-committee, presided over by Shri K.P. Singh Deo, Minister of
Information & Broadcasting, and its report has been accepted by the CABE. The important
recommendations of the Sub-Committee are:

“Every student and teacher should be subjected to a nationally determined physical fitness
test and it should be a compulsory requirement that every student / teacher does indeed pass
the fitness test every year; physical education and sports should be assigned atleast 40
minutes every day preferably, as the first period daily, under supervision of a trained
teacher; every school should have facilities for a number of sports so that students can
participate regularly in one or the other; and yoga practice should be given a great deal of
emphasis in pre-service and in-service teacher training courses.”

The Committee desires that these recommendations of the Sub-Committee be conveyed to
the States for early implementation.

recommends that the Department should make all-out efforts to provide the necessary

sufficient for the purpose and needs to be suitably increased.

3.40 The Committee, is also of the view that yoga is a system, which promotes an
integrated development of body and mind, and should be made a compulsory subject in the
schools.

University and Higher Education

4.1 The Committee. in its Fifth Report, recommended developing ways and means to
make higher education self-reliant, as far as possible. The Committee has noted that the
UGC appointed a high-power Committee, under the Chairmanship of justice Punnayya, to
recommend suitable norms for determining maintenance grants to Central Universities
Deemed Universities and Colleges, as well as to suggest ways and means for augmenting
ae a

recommendations of Punnayya Committee, the Committee was informed that in pursuance
