ll

of the recommendations thereof, the UGC had constituted another Gommittee to develop a |

specific formula in this regard. The Committee is of the opinion that there should be a wider

discussion on Punnayya Committee’s recommendations and an early decision be take on the
~ norms to be adopted. .

4.3 The Committee desires that Universities and Colleges should find ways of generating
funds through financing of research projects by industry and opening of more vocational
courses. The Committee agrees with the view expressed by the Department of Education
that higher education cannot be totally self-reliant. However, any effort made in the |
direction of raising resources by mobilising donations, etc. would not only reduce the burden
on the resources of the States but also create a greater sense of responsibility within the
educational system. But, Government must continue to assist institutions of higher education
adequately so that they fulfil their primary purpose i.e. generation and dissemination of
knowledge. The Committee, however, strongly feels that private investors should be firmly

be discouraged from running educational institutions with a purely profit motive. The
Committee suggests that UGC should evolve norms for regulating, fee structure and to
prevent exploitation.

Rural University

4.4 When the Department was asked about the progress of the implementation of the
scheme of Rural Universities / Institutes, the Committee was informed that the goverhment
has taken the decision to implement the scheme and Rs. 3 crores has been provided in the
Budget for 1995-96. The Committee welcomes the decision and expresses the hope that this
long pending programme will become operational without any further delay.

University Grants .Commission

4.5 The Committee finds that there is a vast difference between the grants allocated and
grants utilised during the year 1994-95. In the Plan, the amount allocated was Rs. 169.5
crores whereas the grants released totalled Rs. 216.00 crores.

4.6 In the case of non-Plan the allocated amount was Rs. 232.00 crores and the grant,
released was 345.59 crores. Explaining this variation, the Committee was informed that
because of essential requirements, which had not been provided in the Budget Estimates,
including the requirements of New Central Universities the grants had to be increased. As
regards non-plan, it was stated that even Rs. 345.00 crores was not sufficient to meet the

4 actual requirement. The Committee is of the view that the resource crunch has assumed
alarming proportions and additional grants are mostly allotted to New Central Universities,
as a result of which State Universities and Colleges are starved of funds.

4.7 The Chairman, UGC, when asked to comment as to whether the allocation was
sufficient, informed the Committee that the grants released were short of requirement. It
was also stated that as against the projection of Rs. 403.50 crores for the year 1995-96, the
Ministry of Finance approved only Rs. 341.82 crores under non-Plan, in view of the ever- — |
increasing responsibilities of the UGC, particularly in the context of opening New Central
Universities, the Committee feels that the amount allocated is not sufficient and needs to be
suitably increased. oF {

4.8 The Committee has noted that on its recommendations made in its Fifth Report, the |
UGC had engaged the services of Educational Consultants India Limited to verify the civil |
works undertaken: by non-grant colleges during the Seventh Plan period. The Committee | \
desires that the study be completed expeditiously and after receiving the observation thereof, |

“suitable action should be taken against such colleges as may have violated the norms.
Indian Institute of Advanced Study

4.9 The Plan allocation for this institute has been increased from Rs. 35 lakhs to Rs. 93



12

lakhs in RE in 1994-95. The Plan allocation for BE for 1995-96 is Rs. 4 cror hen asked
to explain this quantum jump in the allocation, the Department stated that the Institute was
housed in the erstwhile Viceregal Lodge (now Rashtrapati Niwas) at Shimla and the building
developed cracks and was generally in need of special repairs. A programme for such repairs
has been drawn up in consultation with the Intech and the CPWD, and an amount of Rs. 3
crores was likely to be spent for the purpose during 1995-96, the Department added. The
renovation work should be completed as early as possible to prevent further damage to the
historic building.

4.10 The Committee has noted that on its recommendation made last year; as
performance Audit Committee, under the Chairmanship of Prof. V.C. Anantha Murthy, has
been appointed for proper evaluation of the Institute. The Committee desires that the
evaluation may be completed expeditiously.

Indian Council of Social Science Research

4.11 The Committee in its Sth report, recommended increase in the. allocation. The
Committee has noted that in the revised estimates, even though it was increased to Rs. 3.25
crores from the BE of Rs. 2.5 crores, finally the amount released was only Rs. 2.5 crores.
The Committee is obliged to observe that the Department is not making a rational
allocation. The Committee does not consider the Ministry’s explanation that the total
amount could not be released due to resource crunch, as plausible. The Committee is also
given to understand that the actual requirement of the Council for 1995-96 is estimated to be
around Rs. 6 crores. The Committee is of the opinion that the ICSSR was set up for the
purposes of promoting and coordinating social sciences research in the ‘country. The
Secretary, Education and the Chairman, ICSSR admitted during the evidence that the
fuctioning of the Council left much to be desired. They pleaded for more funds to revamp
and streamline the activities of the ICSSR and its regional centres. The Committee,
therefore, recommends a suitable increase in the grants to achieve the desired results.
Dravidian University

4.12 When the Secretary was asked to explain the latest position regarding the proposal
for setting up of a Dravidian University, he informed the Committee that it was a joint
proposal of all the four Southern States. As there was no consensus, there had been no
progress in the matter, he added. The Committee feels that the Department should bring the
concerned States together and put forward some solution acceptable to them. The
Committee suggests that the Department may put a condition that the University should be
located in that State which provides land and other infrastructure free of cost and other
States could have Sub-centres.

TECHNICAL EDUCATION
Indian Institutes of Technology

5.1 The Plan allocation for the IITs has been reduced to Rs. 26 crores for 1995-96 from
Rs. 31.88 crores in 1994-95. The non-Plan allocation has also been reduced to Rs. 120.16
crores for 1995-96 from Rs. 134 crores in 1994-95. On being asked to comment on reduction
in allocations, the Department informed the Committee that the plan allocation was reduced
due to the financial crunch. As regards the non-Plan allocation, the Committee was
| informed that from the year 1993-94, a revised pattern of funding has introduced. The
Committee feels that the institutes should not be starved of funds as it would ultimately
affect the standards of the institutes and recommends that suitable increase may be made in
the allocation at the RE stage.

Indian Institutes of Management
5.2 The Committee has noted that there is not much increase in Plan allocation for 1995-96



13

which is Rs. 12 crores, as compared to Rs. 11.87 crores for 1994-95. When the Department was
asked to explain this, the Committee was informed that from the Financial year 1993-94 the
revised pattern of funding scheme was introduced in the IIMs. Under this scheme, the Institutes
were given functional autonomy and financial flexibility. At RE 1995-96 stage their matching
grant requirement, force majure etc. would be considered and appropriate RE will be fixed.

5.3 The Department has also informed that the proposals for establishing two more
IIMs—one at Calicut and the other at Indore—were under consideration. The Committee feels
that there is an urgent need_to open more such institutions in view of the buoyancy in the
economy and also to counter the proliferation of substandard private institutions. The
Committee recommends that an early decision be taken to establish new IIMs. Location,
selection and other related works may be done expeditiously.
Regional Engineering Colleges

5.4 The Committee was informed that during the last three years, emphasis for development
had been laid on the expansion and diversification of academic programmes and modernisation
of laboratories. When the Department was asked about the. steps taken to bring RECs at par
with IITs, the Committee was informed that a decision had been taken to convert RECs into
centres of excellence on par with IITs. The Committee feels that serious efforts should be made
in this direction. The Committee recommends that the allocation may be suitably increased for
achieving the target. - -

5.5. The Committee also desires that UGC may consider granting the Status of deerfefl
University, to such colleges that have become centres of excellance.
Scheme of Community Polytechnics

5.6 The Plan allocation has been increased to Rs. 30 crores for 1995-96 from Rs. 10.65 crores
in 1994-95. When the Department was asked to explain, the Committee was informed that the
increase in the plan outlay for 1995-96 was mainly due to the revision of the financial norms with
modification in the scope and extended coverage. The Committee feels that full and proper
utilisation of the funds needs to be ensured. ~~

5.7 When the Department was asked about the steps taken to strengthen the scheme, it was
stated that a National Appraisal Committee had been constituted to review the implementation
of the scheme and to suggest for strengthening it. The Committee was also informed that the
Appraisal Committee would look into the various aspects of strengthening the scheme,

. including extension to other areas, as well as for development of linkages with schemes of other

departments having identical objectives. The Committee desires that NAC may complete its
work and submit the report without much delay. The Committee is of the view that this is a
sensitive area where planning requires a special kind of expertise and grass-root experience
which is quite different from what is needed in IITs. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Appraisal Committee should include experts in indjgenous technology, social activists,
especially women, teachers and acadamicians with the desired orientation. There should also be
similarly equipped mechanism for monitoring the achievements and difficulties. The
Department should prepare a programme of action for the extension of the scheme to more
areas and for developing linkages with schemes of other departments.
ADULT EDUCATION . 7

National Literacy Mission

6.1 The National Literacy Mission (NLM) was launched in 1988 and the Total Literacy
Campaign in 1990. In the Committee’s opinion, the NLM needs to be given a further impetus.
Even as the government is seized of the Arun Ghosh Committee Report on NLM, the
Committee feels it desirable to undertake a mid-decade appraisal through National Sample
Survey,.so as to assess the impact of NLM on literacy rate.

Special Projects for Eradication or Illiteracy

6.2 The allocation made for the scheme has been reduced to Rs. 120 crores for 1995-96, as
compared to Rs. 155.75 crores spent last year. The Committee is not happy with the pace of
the coverage of the Total Literacy Campaigns (TLC) in the States which have low literacy
rates. The Committee has noted that in Rajasthan TLCs have been extended to 18 out of 30
districts and in UP 45 out of 65, and there is not much progress in regard to the coverage in
Bihar. The Committee is happy to note that all the districts in MP have been covered. The
Committee, however, feels that vigorous efforts are required to be made to bring all the
districts in the country, and particularly low-literacy States, under the TLC campaigns.

6.3 The Committee feels that the grants allocated may not be sufficient to increase the .
pace of the literacy campaign and hence require to be increased suitably. In those States
where the Post Literacy Campaigns have been started, sufficient allocations should be made
for the campaigns.

6.4 The Committee also desires that TLC and PLC should be implemented through a
multi-pronged strategy. The PLC could be linked up with teaching of skills for self-
employment such as the one at Community Polytechnics and special allocations be made for
the same.

6.5 The Committee feels that the programme should be linked to income-oriented
programmes and greater stress should be laid on the role of media in creating a demand for
literacy.

Scheme of Assistance to Voluntary Organisations

6.6 The Committee is surprised to find that allocation under this head for this year has
been reduced to Rs. 10 crores from Rs. 11.5 crores in RE last year, inspite of concern
expressed by the Committee in its fifth report over the reduction in allocation. The
Committee reiterates its recommendation made earlier for further increase in the allocation.

6.7 The Committee, in its fifth report, had also recommended evaluation of the working
of the Voluntary Agencies. Explaining the action taken, the Department informed the
Committee that it had been getting the external evaluation of the projects of Voluntary
Associations done in various states. The Committee has also noted that the Centre for
Media Studies has submitted its evaluation report on the Voluntary Organisations in UP.
The Committee observes that suitable action may be taken on the findings of the CMS and
the evaluation being undertaken in the other places may be expedited.

Directorate of Adult Education

6.8 Plan allocation for the Directorate of Adult Education for 1995-96 has been increased
from Rs. 4.93 crores for 1994-95 to Rs. 10.37 crores. The bulk of the amount is allocated for
media promotion activities. In the BE for 1994-95 an amount of Rs. 4.18 crores was alloted
for this purpose. The Committee has been informed that this was expected to go upto Rs.
9.42 crores due to spurt in media efforts to build up environment but as sufficient funds
were not available, this liability has to be met from the budget provision of 1995-96. The
Committee also notes that the increase in the allocation is due to the fact the agencies do
not carry the advertisements free of cost. Whereas the Doordarshan charges 1/4th the
normal tariff for National Network Programmes, it charges full rates for the Metro Channel.

6.9 The Committee in this regard, feels that the matter needs to be discussed between the
Department of Education and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and desires that
all advertisements of National Literacy Mission be broadcast/telecast free of charge.


15

LANGUAGES
Modern Indian Languages

7.1 The Committee is anguished to note that allocations for various schemes under the
Modern Indian Languages Division are not being fully utilised. Tarique-e-Board could not
utilise the plan allocation fully during the last three years. Sindhi Vikas Board is languishing
under gross under-utilisation. During last year out of Rs. 60 lakhs allocated on plan side
only Rs. 5 lakhs were spent. The schemes for grants to Voluntary Organisation for
development of regional languages and that for appointment of teachers are also no
exception to this malady. The Department does not appear to make a rational allocation on
the basis of assessment of the requirement of each scheme. The Committee suggests that the
Department should undertake a review of each scheme.

7.2 The Committee regrets that there is no plan allocation for the scheme of production of
University level books and recommends that such allocation may be restored in consultation
with State Book Boards.

GENERAL OBSERVATIONS & RECOMMENDATIONS

8.1 The Committee has noted from the information supplied by the Department that
somes of its wings have not been able to fully utilise the funds allocated. The Department is
still making higher allocations without a rational basis. There must be either something
wrong with the system or there is some slackness in implementing the schemes. The
Department should strengthen its monitoring mechanism to ensure proper and full utilisation
of funds.

8.2 On the other hand, there are certain wings which are facing resource crunch and are
starved of funds. These include UGC, a premier agency for promoting higher education,
NLM and AICTE. The Department should take steps to increase the allocations suitably for
all those wings which are in need of funds. The Department would be in a stronger wicket in
this respect if the disease of under-utilisation of funds in some schemes is arrested.

8.3 The Village Panchayats and Nagarpalikas are coming into existence everywhere. With
this, their role and responsibility are being increasingly felt in every field and education is a
precious. area. Particularly in elementary education, local bodies should be encouraged to
play a major role. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation, made in its
Fifth Report, for greater utilisation of village panchayats and nagarpalikas in spreading
literacy and promoting education.

8.4 The Committee feels that the importance of private funding/investment in education
at various levels is being felt more and more. Inadequacy of resources is a main drawback in
our endeavour for removing illiteracy. The Committee notes with concern that more and
more organisations are entering the field of education with a profit motive. The Committee
recommends that such commercialisation of education must be curbed. On the other hand,
private initiative, as a social service on a ngn-profit basis, should be encouraged at all levels
to supplement Governmental efforts.

REPORT 
 
 I.  INTRODUCTION  
 
 
1.1 The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports is entrusted with the responsibilities relating to 
the development of Youth and Adolescents, and the functions of the Ce ntral Government with 
regard to Sports and Physical Education.   
 
1.2 The subject “ Youth Affairs” is dealt in Department of Youth Affairs of the Ministry.  
The population of the y outh and adolescents is nearly 45% of the to tal population, and the 
number of persons belo w the age of 35 is ar ound 75% of the population.  Addressing the needs 
of the youth and adolescents, therefore, in a comprehensive manner with the objective of creating 
a healthy and productive work force has become very important.  
 
1.3 The Department of Youth Affairs is implem enting a large number of schemes for youth 
and adolescents development.   Programmes of the Nehru Yu va Kendra Sang athan (NYKS) 
focus towards rural youth and vast netw ork of youth clubs and volunteers undertake number of 
activities for youth at the gra ssroot level.  The National Se rvice Scheme (NSS) provides a 
platform for students to enhance their personality through community service.  The Rajiv Gandhi 
National Institute of Youth Development, RGNIYD,  a Deemed University is functioning as a 
Centre of Advance Study in the field of yout h development.  The Y outh Hostel scheme is 
intended to promote youth travel.     
 
1.4 The Committee appreciate s that the Ministry has unde rtaken review of certain 
schemes such as NYKS, NSS, Youth Hostel s etc. through studies done by reputed 
institutions.  The success of these studies is directly related with th e effective monitoring 
mechanism for supervising the activities or ot herwise these studies will remain more as 
futile exercises undertaken by the Minist ry, reaching nowhere.  At the same time, 
Committee is of the opinion that there is general lack of  awareness about manifold 
activities of NYKS and recommends focuse d publicity to attract more and more youth 
towards its programmes.  More and more activities should, therefore, be planned for youth 
living in villages and ru ral areas. The Committee would like to keep a track of activities to 
be carried out under the auspices of Nation al Youth Corps and Rajiv Gandhi National 
Institute of Youth Development (RGNIYD)     
1.5 The Department of Sports of  the Ministry deals wi th “Sports”.  Sports  being in the State 
List, State Governments are primar ily responsible for the developm ent and promotion of sports.  

  
The Government had been  supplementing the effo rts of the State Govern ments through certain 
schemes of financial assistance for sports infrastructure, but these were transferred to State sector 
w.e.f. 01.04.2005.  The Ce ntral Government directly, and thr ough the Sports Au thority of India 
(SAI) is providing financial assistance and variety of facilities, for competition exposure, training 
/ coaching etc., to NSFs with reference to the pr eparation of teams for international events.  SAI 
is also running a number of schemes for the spotting and nurturing of young talent.   
 
1.6 Following the a ssignment of the Commonwealth Games in 2010 in  Delhi by the 
Commonwealth Games Federation, preparations are being made to ensure that all the required 
infrastructure and facilities are put in place well in time.  Action is  being taken to ensure that the 
performance of Indian teams is commensurate with the expectations as a host country.   
 
1.7 A new scheme titled ‘Panchayat Yuva Krid a Aur Khel Abhiyan’ (PYKAKA), recently 
launched by the Department, is aimed at creating basic sports infrastructure, and promoting 
sports activities at the village/sub-district leve l.  Another ambitious scheme, namely, the Urban 
Sports Infrastructure Scheme has been prepared by the Ministry merging four erstwhile centrally 
sponsored sports infrastructure schemes, which we re earlier transferred to  the States in April, 
2005.  The objective of th e scheme is to create sp orts facilities in  urban areas and installing of 
synthetic surfaces to familiarise the players with  synthetic surfaces righ t from the beginning of 
their sporting career so as to  equip them to appropriate skills and training necessary for 
participation in international co mpetitions.  The Scheme is expe cted to be appr oved by June, 
2010.  With two different sets of schemes operating separate ly in rural and urban areas, the

breadth of the country.

III. NEHRU YUVA KEND RA SANGATHAN (NYKS) 
 
  
3.1 Nehru Yuva Ke ndra Sangathan (NYKS) an autonomous body of th e Ministry of Youth 
Affairs and Sports has 501 Kendr as, 28 Zonal Offices and over 3.05 lakh vill age based Youth 
Clubs with enrolmen t of about 8 million volun teers.  Government propo se to extend  NYKS to 
the remaining 123 new districts of  the country during the current pl an period.  Be ing the largest 
grass root level voluntary organization, the NYKS channelises the power of youth who are in the 
age group of 13-35 years on the principle of voluntarism, self help and participation.   
 
3.2 The Youth Clubs en rolled with NYKS work in the areas like education and training, 
awareness generation, skill development and self-employment, entrepreneurial development, 
thrift and cooperatives, beside s development of the body through sports and adventure and also 
through sustained exposure to new ideas an d development strategies.  For implementation of the 
programmes, every district Nehru Yuva Kendra (NYK) has a trained cadre of District Youth 
Coordinators, Volunteers and Youth leaders.   
 
3.3 The Committee observ es that NYKS through  its district Nehru Yuva Kendras, Youth 
Clubs and Mahila Mandals has been actively involved in a number of activities directly affecting 
the general public.  In co-ordination with District/State Health Departments, NYKS are 
supporting Anti-Malaria Prog rammes, National Immunizatio n Programme, National Eye 
Cataract Operation Campaign, De-Addiction, Prev ention of Alcoholism, Organization of Health 
Check-up, Blood Donation Camps, etc.,  as pe r local requirements on voluntary basis.  Country-
wide Mass Awareness Campaign  for Prevention of  HIV /AIDS during Red Ribbon Express 
Phase-I was also carried ou t by NYKS.  Nation-wide Sa ve Water Campaign, Communal 
Harmony weeks are other regular activities organized by NYKS.  Besides that, as part of disaster 
management, drought and flood relief activities are also carried out by NYKS as and when 
required.  The Committee was also  informed that Youth Clubs organize School Chalo admission 
drive especially for girl / poor students.   
 
While appreciating the contribution being made  by Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan in the 
advocacy, social audit,  implementation of va rious Government progra mmes across the country, 
the Committee feels that th ese activities need to be further strengthened.  First and the most 
crucial aspect which has drawn the attention of the Committee is general lack of awareness about 
the manifold activities being carried out by the Nehru Yuva Ke ndra Sangathan.  The 
Committee, therefore, rec ommends that focused publicity so as to attract more and more 

  
youth power towards NYKS programmes needs to be taken up as a priority.  Secondly, the 
Committee would appreci ate if more and more activities are planne d exclusively for the 
youth living in villages and rural areas.  Another initiative which can be taken by the 
NYKS is setting up of Youth Service Centres in the Universities, wh ich can take care of 
needs, both personal and educational of th e young students.  These centres can be the 
windows for building up leadership  qualities, sense of patriotism  and social service in the 
college students.  The Committ ee would be happy if the Depart ment takes up this matter 
with the M/O HRD.

3.7 At present, Nehru Yuva Kendras are functio ning in 501 districts in the country.  The 
Committee has been drawing the attention of the De partment to the urgent need of coverage of 
the remaining 123 districts also under the Programme.  The Committee is, however, dismayed to 
note that no progress wh atsoever has been made in this di rection so far.  The Committee has 
been given to understand  that the time-frame for expansion of the Programme is subject to 
necessary approvals and sanctions of the Governme nt.  For operationalisation of a Kendra, there 
is a staff requirement of one District Youth Co-o rdinator, one Accountant Clerk, Typist and one 
Group ‘D’ Staff.  Fund s are also required for conducting regular programmes and for the 
deployment of volunteers .  In addition, there is a requirement of re curring and non-recurring 
expenditure in the establishmen t of a new Kendra.  The Committee has been informed that the 
proposed expansion would have financial im plication of Rs.49.56 cror e during the remaining 
two years of the plan pe riod.  The main reason fo r delay in the setting up of Kendras in the 
remaining 123 districts is the pr oposal for creation for the requir ed posts not be ing accepted by 
the Ministry of Finance, in spite of being appr oached twice by the Depa rtment.  Instead, re-
deployment of existing manpow er in the new Kendras was s uggested by the Ministry of 
Finance.  The other op tion was to explore the option for out-sourcing wherever required.  The 
Committee is inclined to agree with the Department’s sta nd that both additional posts and 
funds are required for operationalisation of a Kendra in the real se nse.  The Committee 
would also like to point out that already 413 posts are lying vacant under NYKS.  In such a 
situation, creation of required posts for the proposed Kendras is essential.  The Committee 
strongly feels that for setting up new Kendras , functional Kendras be ing deprived of the 
required staff is a solution worse than the problem.  The Co mmittee, therefore, 

  
recommends that the Ministry of Finance ne eds to make available the required funds and 
also give its approval for required posts.  One mu st not forget that youths residing in these 
uncovered 123 districts also belong to the country.   
 
3.8 One of the major bottlenecks in the performance of NYKS is  the large number of vacant 
posts.  The Committee was given to understand th at at present 413 posts in different grades, 
including 168 vacanc ies in the grade of District Youth Coordinator (DYC), are lying vacant.  
According to the Department the vacant posts in different grades which were required to be 
filled up on promotion basis have already been fi lled up by promotion of eligible departmental 
candidates.  Action to fill up the vacant posts on deputation basi s is in hand.  The Recruitment 
Rules for various gr ades in NYKS are in the process of review and revision.  Campus based 
recruitment from institutes of  repute offering courses in social work are also being 
contemplated.  The Ministry has, however, not re sponded to a query wh ether departmental 
candidates are not availabl e in the Sangathan.  The Committee observes that despite a 
number of administrative a nd structural changes under process in NYKS, the large 
number of vacant posts that to o at DYC level is a matter of serious concern.  NYKS has 
already faced a lot of criticis m in earlier selectio n process of DYC post s held in 1996 after 
which no recruitment has take n place.  With the propos ed expansion programmes 
covering 123 more distri cts across the co untry, the present level of vacant posts cannot be 
allowed to continue.  The Committee would li ke NYKS to expedite revision of its 
recruitment rules so that pro cess for fresh recruitment coul d take place to fill up the 
vacancies.  Filling up these vac ancies should be the priority  area for NYKS in case it 
wishes to achieve its objective in real terms.     
 
3.9 It further recommends setting up an adviso ry committee at the apex level in which 
peoples representatives shou ld be included to chalk ou t a programme sheet.  The 
Committee would like the Department to de vise a focused programme on anti-terrorism 
measures under NYKS by traini ng the youth, with a view to  involve them in national 
development so that they could come back to the mainstream.  The very objective of NYKS 
should be to develop qualities of citizens hip and community develo pment and also engage 
rural youth in national buildin g activities, training and rese arch in youth development.  
State Government plays a key role in the suc cess of the programmes and activities of NYKS 
through its volunteers which are identified an d sponsored by Stat e governments only.  
Involvement and in terest of State Govern ments in NYKS programme  is, therefore, quite 
significant.  The Committee would like the Department to conceive and formulate State 

  
specific activities in consultation with Governments so as to increase the level of education 
and general awareness among the youth.       
 
3.10 Youth Clubs and Mahila Mandals have major role in creating impact of NYKS on 
empowerment and development of youth.  The number of youth clubs varies from State to State.  
There appears to be no fixed criteria for opening of these clubs.  The Committee has noticed that 
the Youth Coordinators have the liberty to set up  as many clubs and mand als they want.  There 
needs to be a policy for this purpose.  Further, the functioning of these clubs is also not proper as 
a result of which the office bearers are loos ing interest and movi ng into other jobs.  The 
Committee would like the De partment to review the func tioning of these clubs and 
formulate a concrete plan to re activate and rejuvenate them in case the noble objectives of 
NYKS are to be achieved in true sense.  In fact, the mo nitoring mechanism under NYKS 
needs a complete overhauling to strengthen the delivery system.  The study of IIM,

IV. NATIONAL SERVI CE SCHEME (NSS)
 
 
4.1 National Service Scheme (NSS) is a Centrall y Sponsored Scheme (CSS) with the 
objective to develop character and personality of  student youth in schoo ls and colleges.  The 
Scheme is implemented through the State Governments and the operations of NSS are at the 
University/College and Higher Secondary School level.  The objective of NSS is to arouse social 
conscience of the st udents, and to provide th em an opportunity to work wi th the people in the 
villages and slum dwellers.  The motto of the N SS “Not me but you” seek  to imbibe a spirit of 
volunteerism and community service in the minds  of youth students.  The scheme seeks to 
achieve its objectives through twin approach i.e. “Campu s to Commun ity” and “College to 
Village”, which also helps in de veloping leadership qualities and personality development of 
students.  Under the ‘Regular Ac tivities’, students are expected  to work as volunteers for a 
continuous period of tw o years, rendering comm unity service for a mini mum of 120 hours per 
annum.  Under ‘Special Camping Programme’ a camp of 7 days durati on is conducted every 
year in any ‘adopted village’ on a specific theme.   
 
4.2 The Committee takes not e of involvement of NSS volunteers in diverse activities focused 
on creating social awareness on various crucial issues of public interest.  A number of health and 
hygiene programmes, espe cially in tribal areas of MP, Gu jarat, Maharashtra, West Bengal, 
Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and all the North-East States have been undertaken by NSS 

  
Units located in tribal belts.  NSS has also b een regularly organizing awareness programmes 
against untouchability.   Communal Harmony Week, National  Integration Camps, Medical 
Check-up Camps and School Chalo Andalon are also or ganized by NSS.  Volunteers of NSS 
also play a very crucial role in providing relief during national calamities across the country.   
 
4.3 So far NSS is operational in  251 universities and 42  Boards at 42 schools.  It is spread 
over 14698 colleges and 8174 schools with an enrolment of 32,5 7,104 NSS Volunteers.  On a 
specific query about th e further expansion plans, the Comm ittee was informed that Regional 
Centres were being directed to collect the data abou t the universitie s, colleges and schools that 
are not covered under th e scheme.  The Committ ee strongly feels that su ch an exer cise should 
have been initiated much earlier.  The Committee expects the exercise to be completed within 
a specific time-limit  so that follow-up action is not del ayed further.  The Committee is of 
the view that with the expans ion of higher education in th e recent years and with Right to 
Education Act coming into force, the number of targeted students under the scheme is 
going to increase substantially.   Even otherwise, the cover age of only 8174 schools and 
14,698 colleges shows a consid erable gap between eligible students and those enrolled 
under the scheme.  Details of universities and colleges covered presently under NSS also 
seem to indicate that professional colleges like medical and engineering colleges which have 
shown a phenomenal growth over the recent years have p erhaps remained outside the 
purview of the scheme.  If that be so, Commit tee can conclude that a vast potential of our 
youth has remained devoid of positive impa ct of NSS which has creation of social 
awareness as its main objective, the need of the hour.   
 
 4.4 The Department has inform ed that during  2009-10, a number of reform measures and 
policy initiatives were underta ken / introduced.  A ne w centrally funded sc heme, i.e. a mega 
summer  camp for 400 volunt eers was introduced where under the first Mega Summer 
Camp was held from 22nd  June to 3 rd July, 2009 at the Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth 
Development, Sriperumbudur, Ta mil Nadu attended by 375 NSS Volunteers and 39 Liaison 
Officers.  The other new scheme launched on 26 th June, 2009 was Raji v Gandhi Adventure 
Scheme where under Adventure Camps were organized at various places in the country.   
 
4.5 The physical target envisaged in the Eleventh Plan is to reach the volunteer strength of 55 
lakhs as compared to 32  lakhs at present.  The Committee wa s given to understand that in view 
of the cap on the plan outlay, the Department ha s been constrained to restrict to the current 
strength of 32 lakh volunteers.  The Committee is not fully convinced by the reason given for 

  
coverage of NSS remaining static.  The Commit tee would like to draw  the attention of the 
Department to the Eleventh Pl an outlay of Rs.850.00 crore fo r NSS.  Reasons for Budget 
provision of Rs.52.60 crore in  2007-08 and Rs.86.00  crore each in 2008-09 and 2009-10 
much below the plan outlay of Rs.129.74 crore (2007-08), Rs.156.00 crore (2008-09) and 
Rs.172.00 crore (2009-10)  are not known to the Committee.  Not only this, no change is 
reflected in the provision of Rs .92.00 crore against a plan outlay of Rs. 189.00 crore.  It 
seems that the Department has failed to convince the Planni ng Commission / Ministry of 
Finance about its required Projecti on of Rs. 150.00 crore.  Trend of utilization of allocated 
funds during 2008-09 and 2009-10 lends creden ce to Committee’s assessment.  Plan

stage and expenditure reported at the end of the year was Rs.4 7.31 crore.  In  2009-10 also, 
utilization figures up to 06.03.2010 stood at Rs.56.95 crore against an allocation of Rs.86.00

4.6 Committee’s attention has been  drawn by 66 posts in different categories lying vacant in 
NSS.  Committee observes maximum number of vacancies were of Youth Officer (14 
vacancies), LDC (12 vacancies), Stenographe r (11 vacancies).  Th e committee fails to 
understand the reasons for these posts lying vacant for more than one year.  The Committee was

4.7 The Committee is happy to note that the much-awaited revi sion of cost norms has been

nd March, 2010.  Per Volunteer cost per annum has been revised from Rs.

VI. YOUTH HOSTELS  
 
 6.1 Youth Hostels are bu ilt to promote yout h travel within the country.  The construction of 
the Youth Hostels is a joint venture of the Central and the State Governments.  While the Central 
Government bears the cost of construction, the State Governments provide fully developed land 
free of cost.  Youth Hostels are located in areas of historical and cultural value; educational 
centre; tourist importance etc., where facilities for youth activ ities are available.  Fifteen 
functional Youth Hostels are in  State Capitals.  As on 1
st March, 2010, 80 Yo uth Hostels have 
been constructed and 5 hostels are under various stages of construction.  The Scheme of Youth 
Hostel has been reviewed by the Standing Finance Committee of the Department and changes in 
structure, design and management of the Youth Hostels ar e being brought out keeping in view 
the pace with the new plan of action.   
 
 6.2 Youth Hostels is a nother scheme where plan  outlay for the Eleventh Plan has remained 
virtually on paper during the first three years of the plan period.  What is more  surprising is that 
allocation being made every year in spite of being increased at the RE  stage have remained 
under-utilised by th e end of the year.  The Committee notes that  in 2009-10 the Ministry could 
utilise only Rs.84 lakh ou t of the sanctioned Rs. 3-25 crore up to 26.02.2010.  In spite of 
expenditure of Rs. 2,64 ,69,443/- booked under by that time.  It was cl arified that the exact 
utilisation figures takes some tim e to be compiled as data is of ten awaited from the field level 
construction agencies.  A plan outlay of Rs. 5 crore has been provided for 2010-11 for the capital 
expenditure on construction of y outh hostels in di fferent parts of the coun try as per progress of 
work.    
 
6.3 Elaborating the physical achievements the Mini stry has informed that during the financial 
year 2009-10, construction of one new youth Hostel at Tarn Taran, Punj ab, had been completed.  
Five Youth Hostels were under va rious stages of cons truction whereas 20  (twenty) of the 
existing Youth Hostels have been taken up for face lifting work.  The Ministry has not given any 
reason for delay in completion of these five hostels and it can be pr esumed that at least the funds 
were not the constraints for delay in completing the construction of five hostels.  Details of 
excess grants during 2007 -08 indicates that Minist ry’s projection for incr ease at RE stage for 
repair of the youth hostels on ac tual requirements could not be used.  The Ministry could use 
only Rs. 52 lakhs out of  Rs. 1.25 Crore plan al location for the purpose.  The Committee is not 
convinced with the maintenance level, leave alone the pace of construction of Youth 
Hostels.   

  
 
6.4 The Ministry has shared the following difficu lties / constraints being faced in the running 
of Youth Hostels:- 
  i) Poor management 
  ii) Poor maintenance 
iii) Poor location of some youth hostels 
iv) Shortage of manpower 
v) Lack of funds and poor revenue of hostels 
vi) Poor occupancy of youth hostels 
 
The Committee opines that the difficulties ment ioned by the Department  are inter-related.  
With shortage of manpower and funds, manage ment and maintenance of youth hostels is 
bound to suffer.  Further the location of yo uth hostels is directly  related with their 
occupancy and revenue generation.  Out of  55 hostels appraise d by Youth Hostel 
Association of India, 46 hostels have been rate d poor or bad for one reason or the other.  
The Department has proposed changes in th e management, structure, appointment of 
Receptionist cum caretaker, maximize bed capa city, changes in norms of burnishing youth 
hostels and enhanced financ ial ceiling for renovation and redesigning work of youth 
hostels.  It is a matter of su rprise for the Committee to know  that the youth hostels were 
being run without Caretakers and Reception ists.  How could the management and 
maintenance of youth hostels be possible in  the absence of a Caret aker?  The Committee 
also feels that the pr oposed rate of honorarium for manager and receptionist is quite 
meagre to attract professionally  qualified people.  This am ount needs to be increased 
appropriately.  In addition to  these corrective meas ures, the Committee strongly feels that 
there is a need to take a comprehensive review of all these under-performing Youth Hostels 
based on the findings of Youth Hostel Association of India in coordination with all the 
concerned authorities at all levels so that these Hostels can also be rated as good 
performing hostels.   
 
6.5 The Committee has also deliberated on the pe rformance of Youth Hostels.   In reply to a 
query the Department informed th at recently a concept of performance based incentive has been 
introduced in the compensation pa ckage of youth hostel  managers (previously warden).  The 
Department is also exploring best possibilities to  put the assets of bad performing youth hostels 
to alternative use to serve the in terest of youth / sports department.  The Committee opines that 
performance appraisal of these hostels would certainly help in motivating and encouraging good 

  
performers.  It would also crea te a sense of competitiveness among them and help in overall 
success of the scheme.   The Committee recomme nds that the Ministry should take positive 
and concrete action on the suggestions provided in the study report of International Youth 
Association with regard to the functioning of the youth hostels. 
 
VII. NATIONAL YOUTH CORPS 
 
 7.1 The Ministry has introduced a new sc heme called - National Youth Corps (NYC) by 
amalgamating the two existing schemes – the Na tional Service Volunteer Scheme (NSVS) and 
the Rashtriya Sadhbavana Yojana (RSY).  The scheme would enable young men and women in 
the age group of 18-25 y ears to serve up to two years in nati on building.  The scheme envisages 
enrolment of 20,000 volunteers, of which 8,000 will be deployed in Jammu and Kashmir (J & K) 
and 12,000 volunteers in  other States. This scheme has been  launched on 18th April, 2010. The 
Scheme will be implemented by Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) with the following 
objectives:- 
 
(i) To set up a group of disciplined and educated youth who have the inclination and 
spirit to engage in the task of nation building. 
(ii) To facilitate the realization of inclusive growth (both social and economic). 
(iii) To act as points for di ssemination of informatio n, basic knowledge in the 
community. 
(iv) To act as group modulators and peer group educators. 
(v) To act as role models for the younger people especially towards enhancement of 
public ethics, probity and dignity of labour.   
 
7.2 The Committee finds that the budget allocation fo r this scheme has been substantially 
increased from Rs.28.60 crore in BE 2009-10 to Rs.56.50 crore in BE 2010-11.  The 
enhancement in allocation is due to increase in the number of vo lunteers from existing about 
12000 to 20,000 volunteers.  Further, under the existing Rashtriya Sadbhavana Yojna (RSY) the 
rate of honorarium of Rs.1000/- pe r month been enhanced to Rs .2500/- per month. Government 
propose to deploy four volunteers per bl ock in the districts where Kendra of NYKS has been 
established.  The scheme propose to deploy 870  volunteers in 435 blocks of North Eastern 
States. 
 

  
7.3 The Committee appreciates the idea of combining these schemes as both were working 
towards nation-building through volunteers.  It is satisfying to note that 8000 volunteers out of 
20,000 would be deployed in  Jammu & Kashmir, a State wh ere it is very important to 
bring the youth into mainstream and inculcate in them  the feeling of national building.  
The proposal to deploy a sizeab le number of volunteers in North East Stat es would help in 
arresting the sense of alienation which has cropped up amongst the citizens of this area due 
to alleged neglect of the regio n over the years.  The Committ ee would like to keep a watch 
on the implementation of this useful scheme.

XI. PANCHAYAT  YUVA  KRIDA  AUR  KHEL ABHIYAN (PYKKA)
 
 
11.1 Launched in 2008-09, the sche me aims to provide basic sports infrastructure in all village 
and block Panchayats of the coun try over a period of 10 years. Under the Scheme, village/block 
Panchayats receive one-time seed capital grant of       Rs.1 lakh / Rs.5 lakh each, for establishing 
a playing field with basic facilities.  The state share in this is 25 per cent for normal States and 10 
per cent for special catego ry States.  In addition, village Panchayats are given annual acquisition 
grant for procuremen t of sports equipment an d annual operational grant to meet the operational 
expenses of non-competition nature @ Rs.10,000/- and Rs.12,000/- per annum, respectively, and 
block Panchayats are @ Rs. 20,000/- and Rs. 24,000/-, respectively.   
 

  
11.2 The Planning Commission has sanctione d Rs. 1500 crore for XIth  Plan for the scheme. 
The total requirement of funds for XIth and XIIth Plan periods is estimated to be Rs. 4500 crore. 
The Committee was informed  that budgetary allocatio n during the first thre e years of XIth Plan 
has been Rs. 295 crore which was reduced to Rs. 237 crore at RE stage.   The Committee finds 
that during 2008-09, fina ncial assistance of Rs. 250.77 cror e was sanctioned to 24 States for 
creation of sports facilities in 22,854 village panchayats and 601 block panchayats. However, the 
budget allocation of Rs. 125 crore (BE) including allocation for North-Eastern States for the year 
2008-09 was reduced to  Rs.92 crore at RE stage. The en tire allocation of Rs. 92 crore was 
utilized during 2008-09. Funds amounting to Rs.83.85 crore were  released to 19 States for 
creation of sports infrastructure / sports faci lities and Rs.8.15 crore were released to SAZ for 
conduct of Annual Sports  Competition in States / UTs. During the year  2009-10, allocation of 
Rs.160 crore was provided at BE stage, which wa s reduced to Rs. 135 cror e at RE stage. During 
this year funds amounting to Rs. 105 crore have been released to the states for creation of Sports 
infrastructure sports facilities and Rs. 30 crore to Sports Authority of India for conduct of Annual 
Competitions in the Stat es/UTs. As such the enti re allocation of Rs. 135 cr ore has been utilized. 
During 2010-11 an allocation of Rs.413 cror e has been made for PYKKA . Thus total allocation 
of Rs.650 crore in the first four years of the Eleventh Plan period has been made against an 
outlay of Rs.1500 crore.  The Ministry has claimed that it has utilized 100 percent of allocation.  
 
11.3   According to the Ministry the shortfall between approved outlay and actual allocation is 
not within their control.The Committee treats the Ministry's argument that the shortfall between 
projected outlay and budgetary allocation is not within their control as  undesirable and uncalled 
for. The fact remains th at the Planning Commis sion had approved Rs.1500 crore for the scheme 
for Eleventh Plan pe riod out of which  th e Ministry could utilize only Rs.227 crore in first three 
years of the plan period.  It was the Department  of Sports wh ich conceptualiz ed the scheme, 
approached the Planning Commissi on with its projections and th ereafter the onus remained with 
that Department to prepare a sustainable action  plan worth achieving the physical as well as 
financial targets, year-wise, wh ile implementing the scheme. The Department has to accept that 
the launch of the scheme which delayed leading to loss of precious first y ear of Eleventh Plan 
period.  The Ministry may be part ially correct in claiming 100 per cent utilization of fund out of 
the allocated funds bu t fact remains that the financial discip line with regard to projected outlay 
for Eleventh Plan could not be adhered to.  On the one hand the Ministry expresses a huge cry 
and grouse for cut in their projections by the Planning Commi ssion whereas in the case of 
PYKKA the projections approved by the Pla nning Commission have  remained grossly 
underutilized. The Committee feels that important schemes like PYYKA with its noble 

  
objectives to provide infrastr ucture in rural areas, which ha ve so far remained utterly 
neglected, cannot be operated, with such a shaky and casual approach. Be that as it may 
be, there are still two full financial years available within  E l e v e n t h  P l a n  period for the 
Ministry to make up the time lost and im plement the scheme in a mission mode. The 
implementing agencies would h ave to exhibit the extra level of commitment and vigour in 
achievement of targets so that the shortfalls so far noticed in  the delivery of performance 
are bridged. The Committee hopes that the Department would ad opt a proactive and 
pragmatic approach for better performance during the remaining period of plan.     
 
XII. PROMOTION OF SPORTS AMONG DISABLED.  
 
12.1    The scheme for promotion of sports among Disabled aims at bringing up disabled 
sportspersons in the mainstream of sports at nati onal / international level.  The scheme seeks to 
cover special coaching and training requirements of the target groups, organizing competitions at 
district, State and national level & participation in international competitions and other need-
based specialized support.   
 
12.2    The Committee is not aware about the date of approva l given by the Apex Committee 
to 61 schools.  But fact ual position is that out of 61 schools approved, 1
st Instalment of 
sanctioned grant could be released to on ly 6 schools on 31 st March, 2010.  The Committee has 
been informed that assi stance to remaining schools will be released during the financial year 
2010-11 out of funds amoun ting to Rs.9.52 crore allocated for the year.  Th e Committee finds 
that during first three years of 11 th Plan a provision of Rs. 5 crore kept every year for first three 
years of the Plan has remained unutilized.  The on ly reason for such a st ate of affairs was that 
during this period the existing scheme was being recast.  The Committee has been monitoring the 
working of the previous scheme meant for the mo st marginalized section of the society while 
earlier scheme had virtually remained on paper all these years.  When finally it was realized that 
there was a need for recasting of the scheme, protracted process for the same got started.  It took 
almost an entire plan period to get the scheme finally approved by all concerned.  As admitted by 
the Department itself, it has taken about one and a half year in getting the scheme approved from 
the date draft sc heme was prepared.  Draft scheme was formulated in July, 2008.  It took more 
than six months to get the Draft Note circulat ed for inter-ministerial consultation amongst the 
concerned Ministries/Departments for comments on 30.01.2009.  Meeting of SFC could be held 
on 15.04.2009.  However, due to cropping up of some practical pr oblems with regard to 
implementation of the scheme, a revised draft had to be appr oved by SFC on  23.09.2009.  

  
Finally, revised scheme was communicated to States / UTs, NSFs, IOA,  etc. on 16.11.2009. The 
Committee notes that in response to Ministry’s notice inviting applicatio ns from schools a total 
number of 142 applications we re received in the Departme nt.  The Apex Committee after 
consideration of applic ations in terms of liability crit eria has recommended 61 schools for 
assistance for engagement of coaches on contract basis and procurement of sports equipment. 
 
12.3    The Committee can only  hope that the last two years of the Eleventh  Plan will see 
launch of this much-awaited sche me in the real sense with opti mum and judicious utilization of 
allocated funds.  The Committee expresses its displeasure over the casual manner in which 
the scheme is being handled.  It strongly f eels that the scheme fo r Sports and Games for 
disabled needs to reach the targ eted beneficiaries.  One must not forget that creation of 
exclusive sports facilities for the disabled not only would help  in boosting the confidence 
level of sportspersons who are not at the same level as normal sportspersons for no fault of 
theirs but would also indirectly help in bringing them in the mainstream of society.   
 
XIII. URBAN SPORTS IN FRASTRUCTURE SCHEME
 
 
13.1   An Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme has been prepared in the Ministry and action is 
underway for obtaining the approval of the competent authority.  This scheme is expected to be 
approved by June, 2010.  The scheme has b een prepared me rging four erst while centrally 
sponsored sports infrastructure schemes viz. (i) Gr ants for creation of spor ts infrastructure; (ii) 
Grants for installation of synthetic surfaces; (iii) Grants for promotion of sports in universities 
and colleges (iv) Grants to rural schools.  These four sche mes were transferred to the State 
Governments w.e.f. 1st April, 2005.  The objective of the new scheme is to create sports facilities 
in urban areas and inst alling of synthetic su rfaces to familiarize the players with synthetic 
surfaces right from the beginning of their sporting career so as to equip them to appropriate skills 
and training necessary for participation in internat ional standard competitions.  According to the 
Ministry the erstwhile sports infrastructure schemes involved committed liabilities worth Rs. 
60.51 crore for projects approved prior to 1st April, 2005.   
 
13.2    The Ministry has clar ified that since the scheme coul d not be formulat ed during 2009-
10 no provision was kept at RE stage.  A plan outlay of Rs. 93 crore has been , however, kept in 
BE 2010-11 for assistance to be prov ided for creation of urban sports infrastructure in States and 
development of play fields. 

  
13.3   In the reply to a query seeking distinctiv e features of the new sc heme compared with the 
erstwhile schemes the Mi nistry clarified that there was no  major problem areas with earlier 
schemes which were transf erred to state sectors on  the ground that sports is a state subject.  
However, subsequently Planning  Commission on pers uasion from the Mini stry and the State 
Governments acknowledge the need to have a scheme for providi ng central assistance for the 
creation of sports infrastructure in urban ar eas.  With regard to the release of committed 
liabilities of the erstwhile schemes the Planni ng Commission has assu red to earmark those 
liabilities in Additional Central Assistance (ACA) of the concerne d states.  So far as selection of 
proposals from State Governments are concerned the Department will ensure that urban areas not 
having sport facilities ar e given preference provid ed that they meet th e requirements of the 
scheme. 
 
13.4    The proposal to  transfer the centrally sponsored schemes to th e state has never been 
acceptable to the Committee.  In fact the Ministry was cautioned time and again that states would 
not be able to bear the financial burden on creating infrastructure, despite the fact that sports is a 
state subject.  The Committee is satisfied that the Ministry has taken its view points seriously and 
convinced the Planning Comm ission for keeping some provision of central assi stance to states.   
Planning Commission’s agreement to adjust those liabilities under ACA of the concerned states 
vindicated the stand taken by the Committee.  The Committee hopes that the States would get the 
share of Central assist ance under ACA to take care of the expenses in curred on the erstwhile 
schemes approved before 2005.  The Committee would appreciate if the Department plays a 
proactive role in monitoring the completion of all the pending proj ects in the erstwhile 
schemes for want of funds all these years.  The Committee is also hopeful that the new 
scheme would get the approval within the time  frame indicated by the Ministry so that 
necessary funds for infrastructure projects in urban areas could be released in time. 
 
XIV. NATIONAL SPORTS DEVELOPMENT FUND
 
 
14.1    National Sports Development Fund was instituted by the Central Gove rnment in 1998 
for mobilizing resources from non-Government sources including the private or corporate sectors 
and NRIs with Government providing matching gran t for the promotion of sports in the country.  
As per the information made av ailable to the Committ ee a contribution of Rs. 55.40 crore has 
been made by the private sector  which included some banks, PSUs, private companies and some 
individuals. 
 

  
14.2   A provision of 15 crore has been kept  in BE 2010-11 as matc hing grant towards the 
fund.  In reply to a query about reduced ou tlay in RE 2009-10 the Depa rtment clarified that the 
same has been decreased due to considering over riding requirements of funds for Sports 
Authority of India and scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations. 
 
14.3    The Committee is not satisfied with the maintenance and operation of the fund.  
The Committee finds that the contribution from private sector has been negligible and no 
NRI has come forward for this noble cause.  The Ministry’s argument that many private 
sector entities and NRIs assist the sports persons and sports ac tivity directly in their own 
independent way cannot be denied.  But it is also very obvious that the failure of the 
Department in mobilizing private contribution indicates that necessary serious efforts have 
not been made to motivate pr ivate entities particularly big business houses through 
different Chambers of Commerce.  The Depar tment did not even co ntemplate to use the 
Pravasi Diwas platform for ra ising contributions from NR Is.  Another discouraging 
development noticed by the Committee is that  the Department has managed only 50 per 
cent matching grants of the total corpus in NSDF.  The Committee is  not ready to buy the 
argument of the Department that contribution is made by it in a phased manner depending 
on overall approved budget of  the department.  It rather reflects the somewhat casual 
approach of the Department towards this v ery important corpus, which if successfully 
handled could generate sizeable funds which can benefit our meritori ous sportspersons.  
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the matchi ng contribution from the 
Government should be released in the current financial year itself.

create awareness of the Welfare Fund. 
 
XVI. SCHEME  OF PENSION TO  MERITORIOUS SPORTSPERSONS
 
 
16.1  Scheme of Pension for Me ritorious sportspersons  launched in  1994 is one of the main 
components of Umbrella Scheme of  Incentives to sports persons.  All those Indian sportspersons 
of 30 years who have won gold/silver/br onze medal in Olympic Games, World Cup / 
Championships, Asian/Commonweal th/Paralympic Games and have retired from active sports 
are eligible for pension.   
 
16.2     The Committee notes th at 525 sportspersons are at present drawing pension.  Rates of 
pension have also been revised w.e.f. 01.07.2008.  A provision of Rs.7.50 crore has been kept for 
this Scheme for 2010-11.  The Co mmittee has been given to under stand that proposals as and 
when received are covered under the Scheme.  The Committee strongly feels that with eligibility 
of pension is based on a very specific criteri a of performance based on winning of medals, 
sanction of pension should also be automatic.  Wh ere is the need for wai ting for applications for 
pension to come?  The Committee al so notes that so far award of pension is rest ricted to only 
those sportspersons who have participated in in ternational sports events.  The Committee is of 
the view that this Scheme n eeds to be extended to those sp ortsperson, who win medals in 
various national championships.  Such an init iative would indirectly lead to drawing more 
and more young talent towards sports  
 

  
 XVII.   NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP FOR WOMEN 
 
17.1     Under this Sche me, assistance is being prov ided to hold a nnual National 
Championships for Women in vari ous sports discipline s.  For the past ma ny years the budget 
allocation for this scheme has remained static.  The Committee ha s observed that an amount of 
Rs. 1.10 crore has been sanctioned for 2010-11 even when the same amount remained unutilized 
during 2009-10.  The Ministry has informed that it has been decided to subsume this scheme into 
Panchayat Yuva Krida aur Khel Abhiyan (PYKKA) which will enable funding as per norms 
applicable to other competitions under PYKKA. 
 
17.2    The Committee understands that the Fl agship Scheme PYKKA itself has not 
taken off as it should have been.  Merging other schemes into it may not be a good idea.  
Moreover, this scheme is sp ecifically for women.  Merging it with PYKKA, which is 
primarily for rural areas, this scheme would lose its identity .  In other words, subsuming it 
with a scheme pertaining to ru ral areas would amount to neglect of championship for women in 
urban area.  Any initiatives taken for the promot ion of sports among women can only be done in 
the schemes specifically fo rmulated for women.  Before a decision is ta ken to subsume this 
s c h e m e  i n  P Y K K A ,  t h e  D e p a r t m e n t  a l s o  n e e d s  to review this scheme itself in order to 
strengthen it.  The other viable option could be  that sports disciplines for women in urban 
areas are specifically covered under proposed Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme as a 
separate component. 
 
XVIII.    GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL MECHANISM
 
 
18.1   Lack of foolproof grievance redressal m echanism available to the sports persons has been 
an issue agitating the minds of the members of the Committee.  Given the range and quantum of 
grievances and the problems in  our sports arena, such mech anism does not appear to be 
functional. The country has be en witnessing various controve rsies like those of Hockey 
Federation, weightlifting doping ch arges, selection of players for various national / international 
events, training of sportspersons in India and abroad, remuneration of sportspersons and coaches, 
appointment of coaches, misbehaviour with women sportspersons, medical facilities etc.  The list 
of grievances is never ending.  The Committee pr esumes that more grievances must have piled 
up at the camp venues wher e our sportspersons are undergoing traini ng for Commonwealth 
Games.  Under the present scheme of arrang ements, the aggrieved sportspersons have no 
alternative but to consult their co aches or camp Incharge.  In most  cases their grievances remain 

  
unattended.  Indifference to their   grievances does not argues well for ps ychological well being 
of the sportspersons. 
 
18.2 The Committee desires that Ministry may set up a regulatory body / grievance 
redressal cell that will look into all aspects of  the problems faced by  the sportspersons, 
coaches, sports federations, NGOs, schools, colleges and other sports bodies receiving grant 
from the Government.  This would not only  help in confidence  building among the 
sportspersons but would also bring down the grievances of all affe cted sportspersons / 
sports bodies / agencies implementing sports programmes.   
 
XIX. COACHES
 
 
19.1    There has been acute shortage of coaches in the Spor ts Authority of India as no 
recruitment of coaches has been done since 1998.  The Committee finds that since recruitment of 
regular coaches in terms of the provisions of Mini stry of Personnel & Training and Ministry of 
Finance guidelines could have taken a very long time and requirement of coaches was urgent in 
view of the preparations for the forthcoming international sports competitions like 
Commonwealth Games, 2010, Asian Games 2010 and London Olym pics, 2012, approval to SAI 
for engaging 100 coaches on contract basis was given by the Department.   
 
19.2    The Committee find s that present status of coaches in the country is very disappointing.  
The Committee has been given to  understand that st rength of 1623  coaches way back in 1997 
was brought down to 831 by the Ministry of Finance.  It took prolonged deliberations in bringing 
back the strength of coac hes to 1258 on regu lar basis and 85 coaches on  contact basi s.  As per 
the latest information furnis hed by the Depart ment, there are 1254 re gular coaches and 85 
coaches are working on contract basis in SAI.  The exercise of cadre review including review of 
recruitment rules of coaches is in progress at present and is likely to be completed by 31
st 
August, 2010.  The Committee feels that the most cruci al aspect for preparedness of our 
sportspersons in different sports disciplines ha s remained the most neglected one so far.  
Lack of qualified and experien ced coaches clearly indicates that our country still lags 
behind when compared with ot her countries performing we ll in sports arena.  The 
Committee once again enjoins upon the Department to give  top priority of building up 
required number of coaches.  One must not forg et that in the recent decades things have 
changed significantly in sports also.  To compete with well-trained sportspersons, the basic 

  
requirement is to have qualified experienced cadre of coaches which is also satisfied with its 
service conditions.   
 
XX. COMMONWEALTH GAMES-2010

October to 14 th October, 2010 for which co llective efforts are underway for developing world-
class infrastructure and preparation of Indian teams in various disciplines for the Commonwealth

remained underutilized. 
 
20.3    The Committee has kept  a close watch on the prepara tion of CWG since they were 
awarded to us.  It has noticed lack of coor dination and non-adheren ce to the schedule for 
completion of infrastructure projects relating to  the Games.  Now with the scheduled deadlines 
over, hurried construction may lead to compromise  with the standards to be maintained for an 
event of international level.  Even underutili sation of funds has delayed the readiness of

The Ministry has informed  that work at all the sports infra structure projects for the Games is

Instead of attempting for all events we need to pick up four or five events in which we are
